News.title: Airlines criticise air traffic control as second glitch causes more disruption
News.content:
Airlines have criticised the UK's air traffic control system after a second technical problem in two weeks caused major disruption to UK flights.

EasyJet said Monday's incident "once again calls into question the resilience" of the service, while Wizz Air said there was a "national confidence crisis" in National Air Traffic Services (Nats), which runs the UK's air traffic.

Nats said a "connectivity issue" at Prestwick was behind the disruption across Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England - and had "nothing to do" with a separate software defect at Swanwick earlier this month.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said further issues today "cause even greater concern" about the UK's air traffic control.

When asked by reporters why he won't fire the head of Nats, Burnham said "these are clearly serious issues and they need to be fully investigated".

He added that the transport secretary was taking the issues "extremely seriously" and initially its a matter for her "to get to the bottom of... and why there has been a recurrence."

The underlying issue causing Monday's disruption has since been resolved, with Nats saying it was running at "full capacity" although officials warned of knock-on effects.

A spokesperson said they were now "focused on working with our customers to recover their residual delays and help get their operations back to normal".

Around 150 flights were cancelled on Monday.

Easyjet was the worst affected airline, with 47 of its 670 scheduled departures cancelled, while British Airways has seen 12 cancellations from its 513 scheduled departures.

The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said passengers who had flights disrupted were "unlikely" to be entitled to compensation.

It said the technical issue is "likely to be considered the result of 'extraordinary circumstances' under passenger rights rules", meaning that "although passengers should be looked after by airlines, they are unlikely to be entitled to compensation for delays or cancellations that were directly caused by the incident".

An independent review by the CAA into the resilience of the UK's air traffic control system is under way and the results will be published "within six months", it said.

News.title: Seventeen arrested in Teesside organised crime raids
News.content:
Police have carried out a series of early morning raids targeting those suspected of being involved in organised crime.

Cleveland Police said 17 people had been arrested during the operation - involving about 130 officers including some from the National Crime Agency - across South Bank, Grangetown and Eston, near Middlesbrough, on Monday.

It is part of a high-profile response to a crash on the nearby A66 last month which came at the end of a police pursuit and left two officers dead.

Five men died also died when their Volkswagen Passat went the wrong way down the road and hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle heading in the opposite direction.

The force said Monday's raids had seen people arrested on suspicion of various offences including drugs and assault.

A convoy of about a dozen vans started the operation shortly after 08:00 BST, with roads temporarily blocked by patrol cars.

Officers used battering rams to force entry to several properties as parents walked past with their children on the school run.

News.title: Infantino says he is open to Fifa reform
News.content:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of the governance of world football's governing body and says he is open to reform.

In a letter sent to Fifa council members, seen by BBC Sport and circulated to all of Fifa's member associations, Infantino tabled two reforms to be put to a meeting of the council next month.

As well as asking members if they wanted an external review, Infantino also suggested a "consultation period" where reforms could be discussed.

"First, I will ask the council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of Fifa's current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements," said Infantino in the letter.

"Second, I will propose that the council establish a direct, structured and time-limited consultation with confederations, member associations and relevant stakeholders on how Fifa's decision-making can be further strengthened.

"The consultation would invite specific proposals on earlier institutional involvement, the respective roles of the president, the bureau, the council and the congress, and practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives."

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

His latest statement comes after Uefa and Concacaf - the confederations for Europe and North America, Central America and the Caribbean - demanded Fifa pays $10m to all 211 members from its cash reserves.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Earlier this month, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, told Infantino to release all documents relating to his controversial plan.

The 56-year-old Swiss-Italian Fifa leader will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

Last month, European football's governing body Uefa began preparing criminal legal proceedings against Infantino at courts in the US over the FFE plan, demanding the release of all documents.

Fifa hit back and accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership" in a challenge to the litigation.

News.title: Man charged with causing death by dangerous driving over crash that killed 6
News.content:
A man has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving over a crash that killed six people, including two children.

Shannen Morgan and Shane Roller died along with two of their daughters, nine-year-old Rubie, and Lillie, four, when the family's car collided with a motorbike on the A61 between Barnsley and Wakefield on 21 July 2024.

Husband and wife Christopher and Janine Barton, from Barnsley, who were both travelling on the motorcycle, also died in the crash.

Christopher Cockell, 50, is due to appear at Leeds Magistrates' Court in October charged with six counts of causing death by dangerous driving.

An inquest previously heard that the silver Ford Focus being driven by Mr Roller, 33, collided head on with the BMW motorcycle being driven by Mr Barton, 56, at about 15:50 BST between Staincross and Newmillerdam.

Wakefield Coroner's Court heard the collision happened as the motorcycle was overtaking another vehicle on the single-carriageway road, which had a 50mph (80 km/h) speed limit.

Coroner's support officer Phil Marr told the hearing: "As a result of a head-on impact, the car was spun to the side of the road, where it caught fire.

"It was not possible to release any of the occupants and all four were pronounced dead by paramedics at the scene."

News.title: Watch: Timelapse shows typhoon barrelling towards Japan
News.content:
A powerful typhoon passing Japan's eastern coast is bringing major disruption and heavy rainfall in its wake.

The police are urging nearly two million people at risk in Tokyo and surrounding areas to leave their homes.

Satellite footage showed Typhoon Dujuan crossing the Pacific Ocean towards Japan.

News.title: British Museum bans visitors from photographing Bayeux Tapestry
News.content:
The British Museum has banned visitors from taking photographs of the Bayeux Tapestry over concerns that they were taking too long to view the historic work.

Curators had initially allowed photos to be taken but reversed that decision after long queues delayed ticket-holders from accessing the exhibition.

The medieval embroidery, which is on display in Britain for the first time, depicts the events leading up to the Norman conquest of England and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

Visitors are being allowed into the sold-out exhibit in groups every 40 minutes and told to keep moving along the 68m (230ft) work in one direction.

But people stopping to take photographs along the way was restricting that flow and delaying later visitors.

A British Museum spokeswoman said: "There has been enormous interest in viewing the tapestry, and our priority is to ensure that all visitors have the best experience possible.

"In order to do this, we have made the decision to restrict photography while people are moving along the length of the tapestry."

The 11th Century artwork - which is not a tapestry and was actually embroidered in England - is currently on loan from its home in Normandy, France, and will be displayed in London until July 2027.

British Museum bosses decided that the embroidery would be displayed in a single, straight line, unlike the horseshoe-shaped gallery in which it is displayed in Bayeux.

The loan was confirmed following a Franco-British summit in 2025, following years of planning between the two countries.

Under the agreement, the British Museum is funding the costs of move while insurance is provided by the UK government.

The artefact was carefully packed in a climate-controlled crate and was given a police escort along the unprecedented 350-mile (560km) journey from its home to central London.

Some would-be visitors have criticised the high price of tickets - as much as three times what it costs to see the Bayeux Tapestry in France - to cover the museum's expenses.

Tickets for the exhibition are sold out until 31 December but more are expected to go on sale in October.

Alternately, a full-scale replica of the Bayeux Tapestry is available to see for free in Tewkesbury Abbey in Gloucestershire and at Reading Museum.

His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.

In 2023, he told the Studio 22 podcast: "Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that's all I need to do."

And in this month's American Vogue, external, Kaia discussed her brother's struggles with addiction. She said: "When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone.

"I think that's also why I started to self-identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help."

She added: "My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn't share anything - and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, 'I'm gonna be very human for everyone.' There's only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you're ashamed of them."

News.title: Two pilot whales dead after mass stranding
News.content:
Two pilot whales have died after a distressed pod was spotted off the Northumberland coast.

British Divers Marine Life Rescue (BDMLR) said it had been alerted to a group of about 40 whales near to the shore at Amble at 15:00 BST on Sunday.

It said the whales had been "behaving in a distressed manner typically seen prior to a stranding event".

Due to the tides, attempts to refloat the animals had been unsuccessful, the charity said, and rescue teams were forced to withdraw.

Whales are highly social mammals and are well known for stranding in groups because they travel in large, close-knit communities which rely on constant communication.

There are a range of theories for why beachings occur. Some experts say the animals can become disorientated after following fish they hunt to the shore.

Others believe that one individual can mistakenly lead whole groups to shore.

News.title: Young people aren't snowflakes - mental distress is rising, says head of official review
News.content:
Accusations that the young are a snowflake generation are wrong, the head of an independent review into mental health, ADHD and autism has told the BBC.

Prof Peter Fonagy said in an exclusive interview that there had been a real rise in mental distress among children and young people, with anxiety, depression, self-harm and eating disorders the most common.

He said it was "harder to be young" now given the economic and employment uncertainty young people face, coupled with the challenges presented by social media.

His review was ordered nine months ago by Wes Streeting after the then-health secretary claimed in an interview that young people were over-diagnosed and "written off".

It is likely to feed into government policies on everything from NHS services and benefits to support for young people who are not in education, employment or training.

Fonagy said he chose to speak to the BBC ahead of the publication, which is expected later this week, because he was concerned the debate around ADHD and autism would "obscure" the wider issue of mental health.

More than 100 experts and families with experience of mental health problems have worked on the review with Fonagy, a clinical psychologist and adviser to NHS England.

He said it will conclude that the rise in mental health problems since the 1990s was real, with about one in four 16 to 24-year-olds now struggling.

The data on this is contested as some sources rely on self-reporting, while sceptics argue greater awareness and reduced stigma around mental health mean more people are coming forward.

Some have also questioned whether society was now over-medicalising distress in people's lives â giving people diagnoses when what they are facing is temporary stress that they should learn to cope with.

Last year, the BBC found that many GPs had concerns about over-diagnosis and felt normal life stresses were being over-medicalised.

NHS figures, external show the number of children and young people in contact with mental health services in England has risen by 50% in the past five years.

News.title: 'I see my abusers in the supermarket' - Oxford grooming gang survivors' ongoing torment
News.content:
Warning: This story contains details of sexual violence

Survivors of an Oxford grooming gang say they still see men who sexually abused them, and who have not been brought to justice, walking around the city.

"A shop, a petrol station, a restaurant - everywhere you can imagine - you'll see a man that's done something," one survivor, Sarah, tells BBC Panorama.

Sarah and two other survivors believe "hundreds" of perpetrators are still free. An ex-police detective who led the initial investigation into grooming gangs in Oxford agrees.

It is the first time that Sarah (whose name we have changed) and one of the other women have spoken out publicly about what they were subjected to.

Gangs of men were found to have sexually exploited and abused underage girls in several towns and cities - including Rotherham, Rochdale and Telford, as well as Oxford - between the 1990s and 2010s.

Oxford was one of the places where most of the perpetrators were identified as older men of Pakistani heritage. In some cases, such as in Rotherham, police were accused of hesitating to act out of fear of being seen as racist. But in Oxford a serious case review found no evidence that this had been a factor.

Now, the government has launched a national inquiry to address why vulnerable children were not protected in England and Wales - including whether attitudes to the girls or the ethnicity of the perpetrators contributed to the failings.

News.title: Helen Jenner unveiled by Nigel Farage as new leader of Reform in Wales
News.content:
Nigel Farage has unveiled Helen Jenner as the newly-elected leader of Reform in Wales, replacing Dan Thomas after his arrest on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour.

Speaking on the steps of the Senedd in Cardiff on Monday, Farage said: "I've known Helen for many, many years. She is a determined campaigner."

Farage said he felt sorry about former leader Thomas's "personal difficulties" and that it had been untenable for him to continue, adding: "We could have done without this bump in the road."

Jenner, who served as Thomas's deputy alongside her role as Senedd member for Bangor Conwy MÃ´n, said it was an honour to be elected to the top job.

A leadership vote was held by Reform's 33 Senedd members on Monday morning, and Jenner confirmed that her colleague Jason O'Connell had stood against her.

Figures were not published by the party on Monday but BBC Wales was told the vote was believed to be close.

O'Connell had not been expected to stand, and there had been no vote of the wider party membership.

Speaking to reporters outside the Senedd, Farage said there would be a vote for a new Welsh deputy leader to replace Jenner on Tuesday.

News.title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales
News.content:
Specialist courts to handle cases of rape and other sexual offences will be introduced across England and Wales over the next two years, the prime minister has announced.

Each crown court will have at least one courtroom set up to hear such cases, while alleged victims will be able to view proceedings remotely and give evidence from a separate room via video link.

They will also be provided with private entrances and waiting rooms to separate them from defendants, though this will be dependent on the architecture of each building.

Rape Crisis England and Wales said this was a "significant step forward" that would introduce several reforms it had been requesting for years.

"Taken together, they reflect the urgency of ensuring that courts are fit for purpose and properly meet the needs of victims and survivors, which is crucial to securing justice," the charity's chief executive, Ciara Bergman, said.

Charities have complained that low prosecution rates for sexual offences and delays to court proceedings had disuaded victims from coming forward or pursuing justice.

Just 2.8% of rape offences recorded by police led to prosecutions in the year ending March 2024 and were the crimes that took the longest to investigate.

A prior ONS study, using data from 2017-2020, suggested that only a sixth of the actual number of rape and attempted rape victims had reported their assault to the police, with more than a third saying this was because they felt the police could not help or that the process would be humiliating.

Victims minister Alex Davies-Jones said the new measures were part of efforts to bring down a backlog of Crown Court cases, which stood at 80,098 at the end of March.

Rape Crisis England and Wales said 15,373 of these cases - 19% - related to sexual offences.

Davies-Jones told BBC Breakfast that the introduction of specialist courtrooms "isn't enough on its own" to tackle the backlog and stressed the importance of the Courts and Tribunals Bill to improve "timeliness, effectiveness and also prevention".

The Conservatives say the "long overdue" move should not come with restricting the number of jury trials, which is another provision of the bill.

Under the new measures, expected to cost around Â£23m of the Ministry of Justice's budget, court staff will also be given "trauma-informed training" and a single person of contact will be assigned to each survivor.

From next month, trials will be given a fixed date rather than placed on floating lists in what Prime Minister Andy Burnham said was an effort to "rebalance the scales of justice and put victims first".

There are 84 crown court buildings across England and Wales, containing around 500 courtrooms, and Davies-Jones said the government was determined that every one of them would have at least one specialist rape and sexual offences courtroom by 2028.

Where architecture might prevent courtroom upgrades, Davies-Jones said staff would be expected to co-ordinate a "trauma informed approach" - for instance by scheduling different arrival times and rooms to give evidence from for victims and defendants.

The government said the changes follow Labour MP Charlotte Nichols showing "immense strength and bravery" in speaking publicly about being raped and calling for changes to the justice system.

Nichols waived her automatic right to anonymity in March when she made a Commons speech in which she described having to wait more than 1,000 days to go to court.

News.title: Two arrested over major fire at Folkestone hotel
News.content:
Two people have been arrested on suspicion of arson after a fire at a seaside hotel which led to hundreds of people being evacuated.

Kent Police said a 38-year-old man and 21-year-old woman were held after the blaze at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone on Saturday.

The fire broke out at the hotel in Marine Parade in the early hours and about 280 people were evacuated from the building.

A total of 90 people were relocated from neighbouring Pavilion Court in Marine Terrace following concerns raised by safety inspectors, Folkestone and Hythe District Council said.

The pair who were arrested have been released while inquiries continue, a police spokesperson said.

News.title: Southport killer accused of throwing boiling water mixed with sugar at prison officer
News.content:
Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has appeared in court accused of throwing boiling water mixed with sugar at a prison officer.

The 20-year-old is charged with the attempted grievous bodily harm of a prison officer at HMP Belmarsh, over allegedly throwing the boiling mix through the hatch in his cell door on 8 May last year.

He is also charged with two other assaults of prison officers, as well as possession of a knife or other offensive weapon while in prison.

Rudakubana, who is serving a life sentence for murdering three children at a dance class in Southport in July 2024, appeared via video link at Westminster Magistrates' Court wearing a tracksuit top.

He spoke only to confirm he could hear the chief magistrate, and to give his name and date of birth. He rested his head on his hand during the hearing.

Prosecutor Catherine Pattinson told the court prompt medical attention prevented the prison officer Rudakubana is alleged to have attacked on 8 May from suffering any lasting injury.

The prosecution also accused him of threatening to soak a female officer outside his cell if she did not pass him a newspaper on 6 May 2025, then throwing an "unknown liquid" at her through his door hatch.

Then, on 28 October last year, he allegedly punched a male prison officer in the face. The prosecution said the officer was trying to establish whether Rudakubana had taken his medication at the time.

The offensive weapon charge relates to sharpened stone shards that the prosecution say had seemingly been prised from the floor of the defendant's cell.

They were found stuck to the under side of a shelving unit in his cell. Pattinson told the court that "when questioned by a prison officer, he said that he was keeping them for self-defence".

Rudakubana, who appeared from Broadmoor secure psychiatric hospital, was not asked to enter pleas during the hearing on Monday. He was remanded into custody to appear at the Old Bailey on 19 October.

He is serving a life sentence for the murders of nine-year-old Alice da Silva Aguiar, six-year-old Bebe King, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven.

Rudakubana was also convicted of the attempted murder of eight other children and two adults during the attack in July 2024 at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class.

News.title: BBC removes 11 Mitchell and Webb comedy sketches from iPlayer
News.content:
The BBC has removed nearly a dozen comedy sketches from That Mitchell and Webb Look after deciding they no longer "work today".

The Bafta-winning comedy, written by and starring David Mitchell and Robert Webb, originally ran for four series between 2006 and 2010.

The show recently returned to the BBC's iPlayer to mark its 20th anniversary. But 11 old sketches, including one that reportedly showed the comedy duo satirising racism while in blackface, have now been cut.

A BBC spokesman said in a statement: "This is a 20-year-old sketch show; in consultation with the programme makers, we have included the ones that still work today and not the ones that don't."

The Times reported, external the removed material included scenes featuring the English comic actors as war re-enactors in blackface, a sketch about a contestant on a makeover show wearing a burka and a "tribe" living in a garden centre.

BBC News has asked Mitchell and Webb - who rose to prominence on the popular Channel 4 sitcom Peep Show - for a comment.

That Mitchell and Webb Look grew out of a similar radio show titled That Mitchell and Webb Sound, which began on Radio 4 in 2003, and went on to win the Bafta for best comedy programme in 2007.

News.title: 'Other generations just buried it' - Youths share their mental health concerns
News.content:
Accusations that those growing up today are a snowflake generation are wrong, the head of an independent review into mental health, ADHD and autism has said.

Prof Peter Fonagy told the BBC that there had been a real rise in mental distress among children and young people, with anxiety, depression, self-harm and eating disorders the most common.

Donald Trump launched a Truth Social tirade Monday on skeptics and AI experts who believe the technology is being developed too hastily and with too little oversight — likening them to environmental activists who warned of ecological collapse resulting from global warming.

The president’s comments were the latest in a series of pro-AI sentiments he has shared in seeming defiance with the populist brand that came to define his presidency and political brand in many other aspects.

“The same people that said, “We’ll all be dead in twelve years because of Global Warming,” a name since “reborn” to Climate Change, because the Planet was cooling, not warming, and nobody was dead, are the people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us, that robots are going to attack us, and everything is a DISASTER. This is more of a Hoax than even that of RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, and Climate Change!” wrote Trump.

Trump added that the technology would determine geopolitical dominance for years to come, and dubbed it “SUPER INTELLIGENCE”, part of his effort to rebrand the technology amid the backlash from national skepticism about AI chatbots and the fear that AI could go rogue and take over sensitive national systems. He launched a poll in his Truth Social feed over the weekend asking respondents to vote for either “SuperIntelligence,” “Superior Intelligence,” or “Extreme Intelligence,” the latter of which had been lopped off by Monday morning.

“Whoever wins AI, WINS! We are leading now over China, and everyone else, and I’m going to keep it that way! I’m not going to stifle Growth, of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution, or the Internet, itself,” wrote the president.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump (pictured with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in June) insists that Americans concerned by the unchecked or unregulated rise of AI as a potential threat to human existence are buying into a ‘hoax’ ( AFP/Getty )

This isn’t Trump’s first statement decrying any effort to put guardrails on the use or development of artificial intelligence, frustrating technology experts and leaders in the AI development field who fear both that the technology has been rolled out to the public in existing forms with insufficient guardrails or safety provisions, as well as the possibilities and potential of the technology in the near future, which some directly involved in the field have warned could pose an extinction-level threat to humanity.

The ominous predictions of AI’s potential threat to the entire human race have drawn ridicule from some given the vagueness with which the technology’s actual future capabilities are laid out. But amid a national and international backlash against the direction of AI’s role in modern society, even tech circles and some AI leaders are coming around to the idea that legal and ethical frameworks meant to protect the public are necessary and crucial to the technology’s acceptance among Americans in the short term.

Just last week the president wrote on his Truth Social platform that any attempts at implementing AI guardrails were futile and would stifle America’s economic growth prospects, the main line he has stuck to in defense of his opposition to AI regulation.

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” wrote the president.

open image in gallery Dario Amodei has warned that AI agents are progressing at an alarming rate ( Reuters )

In similar rants, he has attacked AI skeptics as harboring “treasonous” beliefs and even lashed out at Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei for joining calls for federal regulation of the technology. Amodei has warned that within a year a swarm of rogue AI agents could be capable of "taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet," wreaking economic and political havoc alike.

"The Trump Administration has stopped AI 'people' from doing bad, or potentially bad, 'things,' like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a 'perfect little angel' — and we will continue to do so!" Trump wrote last week. "We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies!"

"There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China,” he has also said.

The backlash surrounding AI concerns more than just the technology itself. Land use and the development of AI data centers have become hot-button issues in communities around the country suddenly facing the prospect of massive new contstruction projects resulting in monolithic data center facilities blanketing large areas the size, in some cases, of entire small towns. These massive structures require significant amounts of power and water, leading to higher utility costs for some communities.

Polls show Republican voters to be nearly evenly split on the construction of new data centers for AI companies, while Democrats and independent voters are trending against the issue.

The White House drew widespread criticism for promoting its official app days after President Donald Trump barred three news outlets from the White House.

“Get real-time updates and live events streamed DIRECTLY to your phone,” the White House wrote on X on Monday. It pitched the official app as a way to receive “the news that matters most — straight from the Trump Administration.”

The post came three days after Trump banned reporters from CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House, triggering a lawsuit from the outlets, which argues the ban violates the Constitution. The White House television pool also announced on Monday it would suspend coverage of presidential events in response to the restrictions. Trump said the ban was because of their coverage with critics blasting the decision and saying it goes against the First Amendment.

The White House’s post promoting its mobile app quickly drew a flood of negative replies, with some users comparing the effort in authoritarian countries.

“You’re making Vladimir Putin proud. State run Media,” political commentator Brian Krassenstein wrote.

open image in gallery The White House was criticized for promoting its own news app after President Donald Trump's press ban with some calling it ‘state media’ ( AFP via Getty Images )

“Why would I let your state media track my data?” another user asked. A third wrote: “I'd rather launch my phone into the sun than install a government propaganda app.”

Other critics responded with memes, including one showing Trump’s face superimposed on that of a North Korean state television broadcaster.

The app provides access to official White House livestreams, Trump’s Truth Social posts and the president’s public schedule. It also includes sections outlining the administration’s positions on the economy, artificial intelligence, immigration and other issues.

Other commenters questioned whether a new communications strategy could change public opinion, noting Trump’s historically low approval ratings.

“29 percent approval—and they think the problem is that we need more Trump on our phones,” one user wrote. “Nothing says ‘wanted’ like a government propaganda app nobody asked for.”

Not every response was negative, though. Some users praised what they saw as Trump’s effort to bypass the news media.

open image in gallery After the president banned MS NOW, Politico and CNN from the White House, reporters from those outlets were seen broadcasting from areas outside the White House grounds ( AFP/Getty )

“The lamestream media just stepped right into their own graves,” one X commenter wrote. “What a brilliant move.”

It’s not clear how many people have downloaded the app, which has been in use for years. As of Monday afternoon, it ranked forty-sixth in Apple’s News category.

Soon after the White House promoted the app on social media, Trump held a ribbon-cutting ceremony for a newly installed helipad on the White House South Lawn. No major television network carried the event live amid the television pool’s newly announced blackout.

The White House app did stream the ceremony, however. The video had 994 views as of Monday afternoon.

London Fashion Week (LFW) has had a glow-up this season. With the return of Alexander McQueen and Mulberry, which saw Christopher Kane making his highly anticipated debut for the heritage brand, the schedule was already setting tails wagging before proceedings began. Speaking of tails wagging, special mention to the two adorable dogs walking down the runway at Chopova Lowena. One was sporting a neon green puffer jacket. The other wore sunglasses.

But back to human sartorial matters. Designers set the tone for the warmer climes with eclectic displays encompassing everything from salon-style runways (Harris Reed) and courthouse spectacles (Simone Rocha) to intimate film screenings (Emilia Wickstead) and even an afternoon show held outside the Barbican that had City of London pupils peering out of their windows; thank you, Susan Fang.

There were plenty of famous faces injecting excitement, too, with Joan Collins taking a front row seat at M&S, while Ruth Wilson made an appearance at Erdem, and Paapa Essiedu was spotted at Ahluwalia.

Of course, the biannual affair is ultimately about trends: which ones we’re loving and which we’ll be firmly leaving behind in the previous season. A few stood out, both on and off the runway. Here’s what you need to know to get set for spring/summer 2027.

open image in gallery Scarlet bomber jackets at Simone Rocha ( Ben Broomfield @photobenphoto )

Scarlet fever

It’s fashion’s favourite colour for a reason. This season, pops of red were everywhere, from a standout half-zip crimson jumper at M&S to pops of cherry prints across Ahluwalia’s collection. At Simone Rocha, models’ lips were stained with scarlet, while bone white gowns were decorated with appliqué red roses. Another standout look came by way of a vibrant apple red funnel neck bomber jacket, tapping into one of the most popular silhouettes of the season.

Loud lingerie

There were endless nods to our underwear this season, with the usual contenders paying homage to corsetry – think outsized wings on the neckline at Harris Reed and boned bodices reimagined as entire dresses at Susan Fang. But there were plenty of bonus allusions, too, like at Simone Rocha, who served up a set of deconstructed slip dresses as well as slinky vest tops that came complete with garters primed for stockings.

open image in gallery Harris Reed often references lingerie in his melodramatic silhouettes ( Harris Reed )

Meanwhile, Sinead Gorey hosted a party in the place of a fashion show, with the former strip club setting providing a sultry tone for a presentation that saw every lingerie-inspired look accompanied by welts, while knickers hanging off photo frames and free vibrators being handed out on arrival (the party was hosted in collaboration with Ann Summers). The mood was certainly not one of discretion.

Square-toed or bust

Shoes matter for anyone on the front row of a fashion show. Not just because of how visible your feet will be, but because chances are, the ones on the “frow” are often moving through the LFW schedule at a rapid pace, bouncing around to as many shows as possible.

open image in gallery Hip to be square: shoes with a square-toe were the ultimate footwear item this season ( Getty )

Heels won’t cut the mustard. So, how to make a flat shoe fashion week-friendly? We’ve seen various iterations over the years, from ballet flats to normcore trainers.

This season, the latest front-row It-shoe came by way of a square-toe, preferably courtesy of a Miista boot (very popular among editors this season) or something wonderfully witchy from Lili Curia. Otherwise, a straightforward patent mule will do. So long as the toe is square rather than pointy, giving your toes plenty of wriggle room to breathe, you’re all set.

Tassels on everything

open image in gallery On the fringes: texture on the Alhuwalia runway ( AHLUWALIA )

Usually reserved for 1920s flapper dresses or leather jackets from the Seventies, tassels are being reinvented for spring/summer 2027. The fringing fun began at M&S on Friday, where models strutted down the runway in various tasselled midi skirts. Ahluwalia doubled down on the look, with tassels hanging out from underneath double-breasted blazers and over matching trousers all the way to the floor. This silhouette was replicated on a sportier look, with black tassels swinging over trousers from underneath a zip-up sweatshirt. Alhuwalia also added some texture to its going-out tops, like one royal blue cowl neck blouse that featured a tassel scarf hanging off the back that again draped all the way down to the floor.

Meanwhile, Toga offered something a little more festive, giving its suiting a tassel twist as models’ hands were completely covered by silver tassels popping out from navy blue suits. Those same silver tassels also appeared on the sleeves and shoulders of otherwise humdrum cashmere jumpers, adding a sense of occasion and movement to a standard item of clothing.

No mascara face

open image in gallery Anais Gallagher sporting a bare face on the front row at M&S ( WireImage for M&S )

Those in the know have officially ditched eye makeup this season. It’s rare to see models on the runway with anything but a subtle slick of eyeliner (either that or you can expect giant doll-like lashes as Chopova Lowena did for their collection), but this season saw the bare-faced look copied by top editors and fashion insiders. It wasn’t as if they were hiding behind sunglasses, either, as the stereotypes may suggest.

This season, the prime beauty statement was sporting entirely bare, clean, dewy faces, maybe with a bit of pink lipstick if anything at all. The goal? To have fresh, wide-awake eyes that show the world you managed to get your eight hours last night, which, by the way, is no small feat during LFW. Power moves indeed.

News.content:

Donald Trump’s fight with the media has escalated with the news that five major broadcast networks, ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC, have suspended their pool coverage of the White House.

Their decision comes after the Trump administration banned CNN, along with MS Now and Politico, from the White House for alleged “fake news” and “negative news” reporting.

CNN was due to be the White House broadcast network responsible for covering the White House for the week beginning September 21. In a joint statement the networks said: “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting.”

CNN, MS Now and Politico have filed a lawsuit “to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes”.

Obama said of Trump’s newly introduced press ban: ‘I’m trying to think what would have happened if I had said, you know what, Fox News, you’re outta here!’ ( AFP via Getty Images )

According to the US constitution, the First Amendment states: “Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.”

The once mighty White House Correspondents Association said on September 19 that the “action revoking access for journalists from CNN, Politico and MS Now violates the First Amendment […] The WHCA calls on the administration to immediately restore our colleagues’ access.”

On the day after the ban was announced, CNN’s Betsy Klein, MS NOW’s Akayla Gardner and Politico’s Cheyenne Haslett all reported on having their badges taken away from them after showing up to work at the White House.

Klein’s report on CNN argued reporting would continue and “we can do our job anywhere”. But while this is a commendable aim, it is a wrongheaded argument to make when you are also maintaining that you ought to be doing that job from inside the White House because access is an inalienable right.

Trump’s media battles

Trump likes to characterise his relationship with the press as open and transparent. And yet he has been embroiled in multiple court cases which have seen some media outlets, such as CBS, hoist the white flag, paying stupendous amounts of money for alleged unfair reporting or editing. The BBC is still facing a US$10 billion (£7.4 bllion) lawsuit over a so-called “unfair edit” in a Panorama programme dating back to 2021.

Meanwhile, the Associated Press (AP) is also involved in its own ongoing court action against the Trump government over its banning from Oval Office and Air Force One pool reporting. The ban was imposed following AP’s decision to continue using the internationally recognised geographical term the “Gulf of Mexico” – which Trump demanded be changed to the “Gulf of America”.

Some media advocacy groups are condemning this latest blow to press freedom. Seth Stern from the Freedom of the Press Foundation said: “It’s difficult to imagine a more blatant violation of the First Amendment than Trump banning news outlets from the People’s House for criticizing the government. It’s also hard to imagine a dumber move.”

Given that this White House, in particular the vice-president, J.D. Vance, is often heard parroting the cause of free speech, it is also deeply ironic.

Bad press precedents

Many previous heads of government have clashed with the press in the past but stopped short of bans. Joe Biden restricted the number of press “hard passes” to the White House in 2023 from 1,417 to 975, but as Politico reported at the time, the administration argued this was “about ensuring those who hold them are actively working the beat”.

Barack Obama’s Treasury Department was accused back in 2009 of intentionally trying to exclude a Fox News reporter from interviewing his administration’s “pay czar”, Kenneth Feinberg. This was put down to a miscommunication and was rectified by the administration. On September 19, Obama told an audience at Colgate University which was discussing the newly introduced Trump press ban: “I’m trying to think what would have happened if I had said, you know what, Fox News, you’re outta here!”

About the author Colleen Murrell is Full Professor in Journalism, Dublin City University. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article .

But perhaps the former president whom Trump most resembles is Richard Nixon. One must not forget Nixon’s comments on the press, captured on his own secret audio tapes made from the White House in 1972. In a meeting with his national security advisors Henry Kissinger and Alexander Haig, he said: “Never forget the press is the enemy. The establishment is the enemy, the professors are the enemy.”

Today, the organisations that have oversight of press access and coverage are toothless. There was a time when the WHCA was in charge of organising the press pool rotations and access to briefings and Air Force One. But now it has to bow before Trump’s decisions on granting access to media outlets that extol the virtues of his administration.

According to Pew Research data (2022) only one in six media workers in the US are in a union.

News.title: I tested the SnuzPod 5 as a second-time mum to see if it’s worth buying
News.content:
What is the SnuzPod 5?

The SnuzPod 5 is a bedside crib designed for newborn babies from birth up to around six months, or until your little one starts sitting up, pulling themselves up, or reaches the maximum recommended weight (which is 9kg). It attaches securely alongside your bed, allowing your baby to sleep safely in their own sleep space while still being right next to you throughout the night.

The SnuzPod allows your baby to sleep safely while still being right next to you (Sarah Jones/The Independent)

The side panel can be zipped down when it's securely attached to your bed, making it easy to lift your baby in and out for feeds or cuddles without having to get out of bed every time, which can be invaluable in those early weeks. Like previous versions, it also works as a standalone crib if you don't want to use it in bedside mode, making it a versatile option for naps during the day as well as overnight.

Setting up the SnuzPod 5

One thing I was really pleased with was how straightforward the SnuzPod 5 was to put together. I managed to build the whole thing on my own without needing any help, and the instructions were easy enough to follow.

There are a few different components to assemble, including the wooden frame and bassinet, but nothing felt overly complicated. From opening the box to having it fully assembled took me around one hour, which at nine months pregnant, I don’t think is too bad.

The crib is simple to assemble, requiring just an Allen key (Sarah Jones/The Independent)

Attaching it to the bed is just as simple. It comes with safety straps that loop securely around your bed frame to stop the crib from moving away during the night. Once attached, it felt incredibly sturdy with no wobbling or movement at all.

The SnuzPod 5 also has seven height settings, making it suitable for a wide variety of beds. If your bed has a divan base or a standard frame, it should fit most setups, although it's always worth checking the compatibility before buying.



Design and features

I've always loved the look of the SnuzPod range, and the SnuzPod 5 feels even more premium than the previous model.

I tested the natural wood finish, which gives it a lovely modern Scandinavian feel that looks far more like a piece of furniture than a bulky piece of baby equipment. However, it's available in several different colour combinations – from olive green and cobalt to rouge – making it easy to match different tastes and styles.

One of the biggest improvements over the SnuzPod 4 is the redesigned bassinet. It’s slightly more spacious (4cm wider and 4.5cm longer), while still maintaining a compact footprint beside the bed.

The dual-view mesh windows are another welcome addition. The large breathable mesh panels improve airflow while also making it really easy to see your baby from almost any angle without needing to lean over.

The side of the cot can be zipped up or down to give you easy access to the baby (Sarah Jones/The Independent)

One of the standout features remains the zip-down wall. The zip itself feels smooth and sturdy, and it's quick to use. During the day, it zips back up easily if you're using it as a standalone crib.

The gentle rocking stand has also returned and feels lovely and smooth without being overly sensitive. If you don't want the rocking motion, it can simply be locked into a fixed position.

Another feature I really like is the incline option. It's incredibly simple to adjust by raising one side slightly higher than the other, and this can be really useful if your baby has reflux or congestion.

Another practical feature is the lift-off bassinet. Unlike many bedside cribs, you can remove the top section from the frame and move it around the house. It also has integrated wheels, making it easy to move from room to room without too much effort.

The bassinet can be removed from the frame, making it easy to move around the home (Sarah Jones/The Independent)

The included mattress also feels like a step up. It's a breathable 3D mesh mattress that's firm, supportive and exactly what you'd want for safe newborn sleep.

Compared to my old SnuzPod 4, the overall design feels more refined. The improved visibility through the mesh panels, updated bassinet design and smoother functionality all make it feel like a genuine upgrade rather than just a cosmetic refresh.

Performance

Although I haven't welcomed my baby yet, I've spent plenty of time testing how the SnuzPod 5 works in everyday use, and it's left a really positive first impression.

The zip-down side is incredibly easy to use and feels secure when closed. I can already imagine just how useful this will be during those frequent newborn night feeds.

The mattress feels reassuringly firm while still feeling comfortable, and the breathable materials give extra peace of mind. The incline adjustment only takes a few seconds, so if I do need to use it once baby arrives, I know it won't be a hassle.

The mattress feels firm, comfortable and is made from breathable materials (Sarah Jones/The Independent)

I've also really liked being able to lift off the bassinet. I can easily see myself moving it downstairs during the day so the baby has somewhere familiar to nap while I'm spending time in the living room. Plus, the wheels roll smoothly without feeling flimsy, making it much easier to reposition than I expected.

Everything feels very well made, from the sturdy wooden frame to the quality of the fabrics and zips. Nothing feels cheap or likely to wear quickly.

One last thing worth mentioning is that, unlike most bedside cribs, there’s a built-in storage shelf right underneath the bassinet for holding night-time essentials like nappies, wipes, blankets and an emergency change of clothes for those middle-of-the-night mishaps.

The death of Presley Gerber, Cindy Crawford’s only son, is being investigated as an overdose, police said Monday.

Gerber, the eldest son of Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died September 20 at a rehab facility in Los Angeles, according to the county’s medical examiner. He was 27.

A representative for Presley’s parents and his younger sister, 25-year-old Kaia Gerber, confirmed the death and told The Independent in a statement: “The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time.”

Santa Monica police were called to the facility at around 9:35 a.m. Sunday, investigators told The Independent in a statement. Officers found Gerber dead at the scene.

“SMPD detectives are investigating the death as a suspected overdose,” officials said. “At this time, there is no indication of foul play.”

Presley Gerber has died at 27 ( Getty )

His official cause of death has yet to be disclosed by the Los Angeles County medical examiner. The Independent has reached out to the office for comment.

Gerber was a fashion model who worked with brands including Burberry, Dolce & Gabbana and Calvin Klein.

He was open about his struggles with substance abuse and mental health issues in the years before his death.

If you or someone you know is suffering from drug addiction, you can seek confidential help and support 24-7 from Frank, by calling 0300 123 6600, texting 82111, sending an email or visiting their website here.

In the US, the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration can be reached at 1-800-662-HELP.

News.title: Best gift for new mums and babies, according to a parent
News.content:
What is the best gift for new mums and babies?

The best gift for a new mum will ultimately depend on the person you're buying for, their parenting style and, of course, your budget. I rate everything I've included here, but it's worth thinking about the individual as well as the price tag – something they'll genuinely use is always going to beat a present that's simply pretty.

If I had to pick just one, though, my top choice would be the Rockit portable baby rocker. There aren't many new parents who couldn't do with a helping hand when it comes to getting their baby to sleep, and I love how this simple little gadget takes over the job of gently rocking the pram when your arms – or patience – need a break.

Practical gifts never go amiss, but I'd choose something a little more considered than nappies or wipes. I love the Sunny & Moon muslins for stylish parents, while the Bobbin + Bumble changing mat and Mori sleepsuits turn everyday essentials into something that feels more special.

If you've got a little more to spend, or you're clubbing together for a bigger present, the BabyBjorn bouncer bliss is a brilliant investment that will get plenty of use, while a box of Cook meals might be one of the most appreciated gifts of all – because sometimes dinner is the last thing new parents have the energy to think about.

How I tested gifts for new mums and babies

As a second-time expectant parent, I've been through the newborn stage once already, so I know first-hand what new parents and babies actually need in those early days – and, perhaps more importantly, what they'll genuinely appreciate. Ahead of my new arrival, I tested all of the products in this round-up, assessing them against the following criteria:

Practicality: I considered whether each product solves a genuine problem or makes life with a newborn that little bit easier, rather than simply being nice to have.

Why you can trust IndyBest reviews

IndyBest’s assistant editor, Sarah Jones has years of experience rigorously testing a wide range of pregnancy, baby and parenting products, from the best maternity pyjamas to the best stretch mark creams. Currently pregnant with her second child, Sarah has already experienced the newborn stage and knows first-hand which products can make those early weeks easier, and which ones are simply nice to have.

Ahead of her new arrival, Sarah tested each product in this round-up, considering what makes a genuinely useful gift for both new parents and their baby. As a parent, she knows the practical details that matter, assessing each product for ease of use, quality, design, value for money and how well it fits into everyday life with a newborn, as well as whether it feels special enough to give as a gift.

A much-loved toy store is making a comeback this holiday season.

Toys R Us, to go-to for toy-hungry 80s and 90s kids, plans to open 120 standalone stores by the end of 2026, the company announced this month.

"This is a major moment for Toys R Us as we significantly expand our presence across the United States," Executive Vice President Jamie Uitdenh said.

The expansion will quadruple the brand’s U.S. footprint of 40 stores and marks a major turnaround after the retailer went bankrupt in 2017, largely due to its inability to innovate and stay current with consumer trends.

Toys R Us’s resurgence started in March 2021 when current owner WHP Global, a brand management firm, bought a controlling stake in the company. Since then, it’s opened standalone stores and kiosks in airports and department stores to grab a slice of the country’s rebounding retail toy market.

Toys R Us has fought back from bankruptcy to launch an ambitious expansion plan ( AFP/Getty )

The company did not say where its new stores will open. The Independent has contacted Toys R Us for comment.

The U.S. toy industry has had a rollercoaster five years but is on the way up again, according to industry advocate The Toy Association. Sales surged from $30.4 billion in 2021 to $30.6 billion in 2022, the association said. Sales then dipped below $30 billion in 2023 and 2024 before rebounding to $30.3 billion in 2025.

Games and puzzles, explorative toys and building sets saw the most growth from 2024 to 2025, while plush toys and outdoor/sports toys saw the biggest declines, according to the association.

This year, the industry has thrived despite consumers facing financial challenges due to elevated cost of living and gas prices. Even as consumers deal with financial pressures, they focused their toy spending on mid-tier and premium brands, according to a June analysis from market research firm Circana.

“This trend mirrors broader retail dynamics, where higher prices and more selective spending are driving revenue gains,” the analysis noted. Through April, sales were up 13 percent. Games and puzzles rose 39 percent year-on-year, and building sets like LEGO rose 20 percent.

Squishy toys are all the rage thanks to social media marketing on channels like TikTok, Circana said. The squeezable sensations saw sales grow by triple digits through the first four months of the year.

Overall, the retail industry is expected to generate more than $1 trillion in sales this holiday sales for the first time ever, according to a September analysis from consulting firm Bain & Company.

News.title: ‘42 surgeries in 48 hours’: Doctors face extreme pressure in South Sudan
News.content:
Dr Mathiang Agany had no idea what was coming.

On a humid morning in April, scores of patients were rushed into his basic hospital in rural South Sudan after a shoot out between rival gangs. As the most senior doctor, Dr Agany, a maternal health specialist, had to perform 42 surgeries in just 48 hours.

Working alongside a second surgeon, a nurse and an anaesthetist, Dr Agany, 44, carefully extracted bullets from the vital organs of nine patients.

In 22 cases, he glued together fractured bones; and in four others he clamped damaged tissues shut and repaired torn organs.

Over the same 48 hour period, he also delivered seven babies through emergency c-sections.

“You are tired... but you can relax later,” he told The Telegraph over a video call.

“My job [was] to keep people alive”.

Separate to the ruinous four-year civil war in neighbouring Sudan, the violence plaguing South Sudan is inter-communal, a self-perpetuating cycle of cattle raiding, territorial disputes and revenge attacks carried out by armed youth militias from pastoral communities known as Titweng (“cattle guard”).

Young children were among the victims, including a four-year-old boy, whose leg was fractured by a gunshot, and a nine-month-old baby girl whose chest was grazed by the same bullet that killed her father.

News.title: Afghan medical students face expulsion from Pakistan
News.content:
An educational lifeline for young Afghan women banned by the Taliban from training as doctors in their homeland is in jeopardy after Pakistan’s medical authorities tried to have them expelled.

Several hundred Afghan female students studying across the border in Pakistan have been threatened with removal, amid rising tensions and tit-for-tat exchanges between the neighbours.

The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) which regulates medical education earlier this month ordered medical and dental colleges with Afghan students to kick them out.

Within days, major institutions including King Edward Medical University (KEMU), Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, had ordered Afghan students to leave.

The nationwide order was estimated to have affected around 1,000 Afghan students, with 35 per cent of those thought to be female students.

Provincial high courts have now temporarily halted the expulsion pending further hearings, but Afghan students told The Telegraph they were terrified their careers would be ended.

“The government’s decision aimed to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned female education,” said Sabiha Daftani, one of the 22 Afghan students given orders on September 7 by KEMU in Lahore on to leave within 24 hours.

“The fear is constant and haunting us,” she said.

News.title: Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change
News.content:
But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.

He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

News.title: Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool
News.content:
It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: An A to Z guide to what’s in your laundry detergent
News.content:
Laundry is one of those jobs that most of us do on autopilot. Throw a load of washing and your favourite detergent into the drum and wait for the machine to work its magic. Perhaps you’ve never even thought to ask yourself what chemicals you’re putting in with your clothes.

In the UK, detergent brands are legally required to state the use of surfactants and enzymes (the main ingredients for stain removal) in a way that is easy to understand, but you may see additional compounds that leave you scratching your head.

Here, I break down the words on the back of the bottle to help you understand exactly what you’re putting in your washing. Given that I’ve just tested 26 laundry detergents and developed an app to help you clean your clothes better, I’m the best woman for the job.

Below, you’ll find the most common detergent ingredients listed A to Z. If you’ve got a burning question about a laundry buzzword, I should be able to help. Add any in the comments section below.

Anionic

There are two main types of surfactants: anionic and non-ionic. A surfactant has a hydrophilic head that loves water and a hydrophobic tail that hates it. Anionic surfactants have a negative charge on their head, which is what helps lift soils and stains from the fabric, though they’re not so good at getting rid of oils. They create a lot of foam but their effectiveness can be limited by minerals found in hard water, which is why they are paired with non-ionic surfactants.

Bio

Short for biological, this label means that a detergent contains enzymes. These are proteins that break down fats, starches and grease, so use bio formulations when you need to tackle stubborn food stains. They are effective at lower temperatures but they can be abrasive on sensitive skin. If your skin is easily irritated, opt for non-bio, instead.

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Rangers hero Ally McCoist broke my leg on Australia pub crawl – I feared my career was OVER
Sports.content:
Next

EVER since the idea of writing my autobiography came about, I’ve been dreading this aspect of it — the true story of how I broke my leg.

But it’s been 40 years since the incident and I’m pretty sure enough time has passed for the truth to be told.



The truth is that it was a drunken altercation with Ally McCoist — and it was all my own fault.

Rangers boss Jock Wallace had arranged a tour to New Zealand and Australia for the end of the 1983-84 season.



Our first game was a 0-0 draw against an Australian B side in Melbourne and I had to make do with a place on the bench.

Next stop Brisbane. On arrival, we discovered that Manchester United were also touring there and Big Jock and the United boss, Ron Atkinson, got talking.



It turned out United were staying in a place called Surfers Paradise. It sounded brilliant and, if it was good enough for them, it was good enough for us.

We had been given an evening pass from the boss and everybody was up for a night out.

As the night progressed, we started getting separated. I found myself with Craig Paterson, Ally Dawson and Coisty.

We had left one pub and were looking for our next watering hole. We didn’t have a clue where we were going and found ourselves walking down this really wide road.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

We couldn’t see any sign of the bright lights of a pub, nor how we could get back to where we were staying, the Beachcomber Hotel.

As we discussed our next move, we thought we would take advantage of a grassy area to have a comfort break against one of the trees.

And as we were standing there, I began to joke with Coisty that I was going to ‘wash his shoes’, if you know what I mean.



I never did it, but one thing led to another and, before long, it was East Kilbride versus Easterhouse!

Perhaps, if we had been boxers, it would have been fists up, but we both kicked out with our feet, which resulted in an almighty clash of shins.

As I went down and landed on my backside I wasn’t in any pain, but I immediately knew something was wrong.

The other lads, Craig and Ally, were telling the two of us to get a move on.

I was lying on my back, my legs bent above me and I was thinking about getting up, but then I noticed something protruding from just below my knee.



I put my hand down and that was when I realised the thing sticking out was my bone, which had pierced through my skin.

The lads’ patience was, by now, wearing a bit thin, but as soon as they came over they immediately knew the only place I was going was to the hospital.

One of the lads went to phone an ambulance — the other had the dubious pleasure of going to inform Jock.

When Jock demanded an explanation, they were to say that they hadn’t seen anything.

This left me and Coisty alone, in the dark. He was a bit tearful as the full realisation of what had occurred began to register.



There might have been tears from me, too. I knew that this was a potentially career-threatening injury.

‘It wasn’t your fault,’ I said to him. ‘It was basically down to me’.

But Ally was distraught.

I then looked over and saw a nearby fence. And I knew exactly what I had to do.

‘Right,’ I said. ‘See that fence, I tried to jump it and I never made it. That’s what we’re going to say’.



But Ally was having none of it. He was adamant that, no matter the repercussions, he was going to tell the truth.

I knew that wasn’t a good idea. Ally was on his last warning and Jock’s patience with him was already wearing thin.

Any breach of rules and he was on the next plane home and, believe me, Jock would have done it.



Imagine if that had happened. Who knows what future Ally would have had at Rangers — if any?

Look what he went on to achieve at the club, the goals he scored, the trophies he won, the legend he became.

Was that really going to be put at risk because of some daft incident?

There was no way he should pay such a high price for what was my stupidity.

What had happened was no fault of Ally. It was all down to me.



It was my fault we had squared up but still he wanted to tell the truth.

So I said to Ally, ‘You don’t want to be doing that. You were on your last warning before we left London. No, you can’t do that. We’ll just say that I tried to jump the fence and didn’t make it. That’s what happened. I’m sure Craig and Ally will back that up’.

He took some convincing but, eventually, Ally came round to my way of thinking and Ally and big Craig stuck to the line that they didn’t see anything.

It was a story that would hold firm for four decades!

Big Jock caught up with us in the hospital when two nurses began trying to take off my trousers.



Even they were wincing when they tried to get my trousers over my leg.

It had swollen to twice the size and the bones were making a horrible grinding noise each time they hit.

Then, remarkably, Jock told me what happened, how my leg break had come about.

He said Coisty had told him everything, but, to my relief, he recounted the tale of me trying to jump the fence.

Then he paused. ‘Did Coisty top you?’ he asked.



My brain was working overtime. I was going to stick to our story no matter what.

‘No, I tried to jump a fence,’ I said. ‘It was further away than I thought. I landed on top of the thing and snapped my leg’.

Over the years, I have come to the conclusion that Big Jock knew the truth.



He felt there was some kind of undercurrent between me and Coisty, but I never felt it and I’m sure Ally didn’t.

But, at the time, I was laying there wondering how he could possibly know what had actually happened?

Jock looked at me. ‘Well’, he said. ‘If that’s the story you’re telling, you had better stick to it. I don’t want to hear anything else’.

I needed an operation and the surgeon told me he was confident he had done a good job, putting in a plate and some screws to hold everything in place.

But he didn’t know if I’d be able to continue with football, saying only that it was very much down to me and how the recovery developed.



I always believed I could get through it. I had to. There was no way I was going back on the tools.

I was determined not to let my career finish like that.

Out Of Easterhouse, The Bobby Williamson Story (Pitch Publishing), publishes on October 12. RRP £25.00.
