He stressed that the ticket brings together two crucial pillars needed for governance: private sector innovation and public sector leadership.

“Today marks an important milestone in our collective vision for a more prosperous and forward-looking Adamawa State. In Engr. Safriel Glah, we have found a partner whose distinguished career embodies excellence, discipline, professionalism, and selfless service”, Mr Haske stated.

Mr Haske highlighted that while his personal background is anchored in business enterprise, investment, and youth empowerment, Mr Glah brings over 34 years of public administration, environmental governance, and institutional management to the campaign.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our partnership represents a convergence of complementary strengths,” Mr Haske added. “While I have spent years building businesses and promoting enterprise, Engr. Glah has built an outstanding record in public administration and policy implementation. Together, we offer Adamawa a competent, balanced team dedicated to transforming the fortunes of our state.”

About the deputy governorship candidate

Mrs Glah retired from NNPC Limited as General Manager and Head of Environment, Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE).

A Fellow of the Nigerian Society of Engineers (FNSE), she is widely recognised for her leadership in engineering, environmental sustainability, and community development.

Her career spanned over 34 years in Nigeria’s oil and gas sector (NNPC Limited). She is a fellow of the Nigerian Society of Engineers (FNSE), with a focus on engineering management, environmental policy, institutional discipline, and sustainable governance.

In her acceptance speech, Ms Glah thanked the APM leadership and the citizens of Adamawa State for their trust in her, promising to complement Mr Haske’s vision with dedication and administrative rigour.

“I stand before you today humbled and profoundly grateful. As Deputy Governorship Candidate, I will support my principal, complement his leadership, and work with our team to promote a vision of inclusive development, opportunity, accountability, and sustainable progress. To the people of Adamawa State, I am ready to listen, ready to work, and ready to serve.”

Speaking in separate interviews following the event, the APM National Chairman, Yusuf Dantalle, and the Adamawa State Chairman, Badejo Bello, declared the Haske-Glah ticket a winning formula.

Mr Dantalle noted that the APM intentionally crafted a ticket that balances private enterprise with public governance experience, creating a compelling platform for economic growth, job creation, and institutional reform.

Echoing his views, the Adamawa State Chairman, Mr Bello, stated that Ms Glah’s emergence has provided a major boost to the party’s electoral prospects ahead of 2027.

He expressed confidence that the ticket’s blend of business enterprise and administrative integrity will resonate deeply across all constituencies in Adamawa State.

World.title: Why I still rent despite making money to buy houses — Ola of Lagos
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nigerian influencer and entrepreneur, Waris Olayinka Akinwande, popularly known as Ola of Lagos, has explained why he deliberately chooses to live in a rented apartment despite having the financial capacity to own a house.

Speaking on a recent episode of the KK Show, Ola said he has never slept in a house he bought with his own money because paying rent motivates him to work harder.

The luxury influencer explained that the financial responsibility of paying rent keeps him focused and reminds him that he needs to continue working to meet his obligations.

He said: “If I sleep in a house I bought with my own money, I’ll relax. No! Rent, pay rent make you know say you wan pay 50 million naira.

“Pay, so that you go know say you have to work. If you go dey your house wey you buy. No, it’s fine to stay in your house, that’s my own opinion, don’t let that judge your life oo.”

Ola, however, stressed that his approach should not be treated as a general rule, noting that people’s financial circumstances differ.

“No, it depends on your reality,” he said.

“Some people now, na the car wey dem go buy, go buy them houses. Like one of my mentors online, he said his first car bought him houses.

“Yeah, so look at your current situation.”

Vanguard News

World.title: California declares state of emergency ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Maria del Carmen Portillo de Hernandez, 32, walks inside her tilapia pond to remove debris, which has low water levels due to the lack of rainfall, in the hamlet of El Matazano, San Simon, Morazan department, El Salvador, on September 10, 2026. Animals are dropping dead amid the worst drought in living memory for many Central Americans, who are grappling with the unforgiving effects of the powerful El Nino weather pattern. (Photo by Marvin RECINOS / AFP)

California’s governor on Monday declared a state of emergency as the US west coast readies for what is expected to be a damaging El Nino.

Forecasters say the coming months could bring powerful and damaging storms to the region because of this weather pattern, with the threat of higher-than-usual tides that could trigger coastal flooding.

Governor Gavin Newsom said the state needed to get ahead of problems instead of waiting for them to happen.

“This action is about giving communities the support they need, giving first responders the tools to do their jobs, and giving families the confidence that their state is ready,” he said.

“We are preparing for this El Nino early because every Californian deserves to be safe in their home, connected to their community, and protected when severe weather comes.”

Monday’s declaration is procedural and intended to make it easier for state agencies to access resources, and to pre-position flood-fighting supplies like sandbags and pumps.

The proclamation also prepares the California National Guard to support flood response, search-and-rescue, engineering, and logistics missions when needed, officials said.

El Nino is the warming phase of a natural cycle in the tropical Pacific, known as the El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), and comes along every two to seven years.

It sets in when east-to-west trade winds ease, allowing warm water which normally collects in the western Pacific Ocean to slide back east and rise to the surface.

When those warmer-than-average surface temperatures last for a few months, they cause more storms and clouds over the region, which in turn cause ripple effects through the entire global atmosphere: hotter and drier conditions in some places, cooler and wetter in others.

Human-caused climate change increases El Nino’s impacts. A warmer atmosphere holds more moisture, so El Nino-linked rains can turn more extreme. It also dries out soil, deepening drought where El Nino brings it.

This year’s El Nino has a 69 percent chance of becoming the strongest on record, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and is already unleashing extreme weather across the globe even though it is not expected to peak until October-December.

California’s coastline has already been battered by storms that have damaged or destroyed homes.

Coastal erosion also forced the cancellation of a music festival in Santa Monica that had been set to feature The Killers, Olivia Dean and Jack White.

AFP

World.title: IHRC releases names of 37 miners who died in NSCDC custody
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

The International Human Rights Commission IHRC has released the names of suspected illegal miners who died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC in Niger State.

The victims were among scores of suspects arrested during operations conducted on September 15 and 16 around Lt Gen Mohammed Inuwa Wushishi Estate in Minna, the Niger State capital.

The state’s NSCDC Commandant at the time, Suberu Aniviye, had said in a statement that scores of the detained suspects were found dead in the early hours of Thursday following a suspected outbreak of disease.

Following the development, the Federal Government suspended the Niger State NSCDC commandant and ordered a full investigation into the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

According to a report by The Cable, the IHRC said it had compiled a list of the 37 deceased, disclosing that the organisation obtained the initial list from the records of the General Hospital, Minna. The International Peace Ambassador at the IHRC, Awaisu Giwa, said the names were provided by the mortuary attendant on the instruction of the hospital’s Chief Medical Director, adding that four additional names had since been added to the list after relatives of victims whose names were not initially recorded approached the commission.

“We got the list from the CMD of the general hospital. It was written by the mortuary attendant for us, but we are going to the hospital tomorrow for the list to be on the official letterhead of the hospital. The CMD was the one who instructed the mortuary attendant to give us the names. Some people whose relatives were missing are beginning to report in our office”, Giwa said.

Giwa said the list would also be used to facilitate compensation for families of those who died in the incident.

The names of the deceased, as compiled by the IHRC and cross-checked against the General Hospital’s records, are: Ibrahim Sani, Fahad Sa’adu, Abdulsalam Ismail, Usman Aliyu, Abubakar Alhaji, Sani Nasir, Sanusi Khalid, Ahmad Aliyu, Safiyanu Abdullahi, Suleiman Dantala, Idris Haruna, Sani Yakubu, Safiyanu Abubakar, Abdullahi Abubakar, Abubakar Musa, Abdul Mudassir, Suleiman Lawal, Usman Abdullahi, Samuel Sambo, Ibrahim Musa, Yusuf Nasiru, Umar Lawal, Isyaku Amisu, Bissallah Adamu, Abdulbari Suleiman, Shafisu Lado, Usman Ahmad, Usman Ibrahim, Sani Isyaku, Musa Ibrahim, Idris Bashir, Kabiru Suleiman and Emmanuel Emeka.

Four additional names, said not to have been included in the General Hospital’s list, were also provided by the IHRC: Mu’awiya AbdulKarim, Abdul Gafar Abubakar, Usman Haruna and Yaro Salihu Soba.

World.title: Tinubu understands my Rainbow Coalition – Wike
World.content:
Minister Nyesom Wike and President Bola Tinubu.

By Omeiza Ajayi

Federal Capital Territory FCT minister, Nyesom Wike, has said President Bola Tinubu fully understands the concept behind his Rainbow Coalition project, insisting that the sustained attacks on the initiative are being driven by Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, whose ambition to become Senate President ahead of the expiration of his tenure has fuelled the crisis.

Speaking during a live interview on TVC on Monday night, Wike, who is also the national leader of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP, dismissed claims that the Rainbow Coalition posed any threat to President Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the criticism as coming from someone seeking to cause crisis within the system rather than tell Nigerians the truth.

He said, “In a country like this, somebody whose tenure will be expiring in 10-11 months time, now because of wanting to change or cause crisis within the system, wants run for election to the Senate Presidency, and without telling people the truth, he Is now saying the Rainbow Coalition is a problem. How will the Rainbow Coalition be a problem? Mr President, everyone in all the states, support the President. You want to run for Senate, House of Reps, Governorship? it is your internal affair,” Wike said.

He explained that the coalition’s only position was that Nigerians across parties should support Tinubu’s re-election, while leaving room for members to pursue their own political ambitions at the state and National Assembly levels. “All they want me to do is to say, since they are supporting the President, nobody should run for National Assembly, nobody should run for State Assembly, nobody should run for Governorship. Where do you see that happening? Then they will call me to tell me, can we produce candidates of your party? Come on, who does that? No, sorry, I don’t,” he said.

Wike also dismissed reports that the President had agreed to concede nine states to him as part of the coalition arrangement, challenging those spreading the claim to name the states in question.

“First of all, did they tell you the nine states? No, they didn’t tell me. You see, we owe Nigerians the truth. Tell them the truth. Which are those nine states? State A, state B, state C?” he said, insisting that such propaganda could not have come from anyone genuinely working for the President’s re-election.

The minister pointed to the President’s position on creation of state police and the South-East presidency question as evidence of Tinubu’s boldness in tackling issues previous leaders avoided.

“Mr President has taken the bull by the horns and said, state police should be considered. People are saying, to solve our security problem, we must have a state police. Mr President has come out boldly to say, I am in support of what they are saying. We must implement it. How many people have done that?” he said, adding that he had never seen a president as committed to devolving power to sub-national governments.

“I have never seen, with all due respect, a man who believes that power should go down, make the rural areas, local governments, state governments have funds to develop. I have never seen that happen. I was governor. I know what I suffered.”

On suggestions that his coalition activities were positioning him to succeed Tinubu in 2031, Wike again rejected the claim, maintaining that his interests could not collide with the President’s since Tinubu would not be seeking re-election at that point.

He said questions about his ambition were misplaced given his political standing. “By the grace of God, I don’t think there’s anything a politician wants today that President Tinubu has not made me to achieve. And people should stop talking about ambition, ambition.”

Wike further argued that resistance to the Rainbow Coalition stemmed from a fear of losing control over key National Assembly positions rather than genuine concern for the President’s interest.

“For Mr President to win, not only a party. It’s not only APC supporting President, PDP supporting him, Labour supporting him, this party supporting him. You’re not happy. Simply because you know that you will not be in control. You are not going to be the one that will be in control of who will be Senate President? You want to make President to be a lame President. It will not work. President must still have that hand,” he said.

Asked whether he had reached out to the roughly three All Progressives Congress (APC) governors he does not appear to trust, Wike said there was no need for such moves in the absence of a genuine issue, adding that Tinubu had not called him over the matter because none existed. “Why would the President call me, is there any issue? The President will call you when there are issues, when he knows, look, this will give me problems. Of course, he is President and a politician. Who doesn’t know him that he’s a master strategist in this game?” he asked.

The minister drew a distinction between the governors he considered cordial and those he accused of manufacturing grievances against him, describing the Governor of Kwara State, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, as very timid.

“I don’t carry anybody’s fight. You have a problem with Saraki? You go and fight with Saraki. Why do you, as a politician, fall into the trap of Saraki? He (AbdulRazaq) carries propaganda every day against me.

“Have you forgotten all these people who fought me? When this fight was going on, they supported my colleagues and told my colleagues to deal with me, that enough is enough of me. My colleagues joined them. Now I have won. And now you want something from me? You say you want me to be a houseboy. Houseboy for what? That’s not possible. The point is that go and fight your fight,” he declared.

World.title: NLC demands independent investigation into death of 37 mines
World.content:
Joe Ajaero, NLC President

The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has demanded a thorough, transparent and independent investigation into the deaths of 37 persons in NSCDC custody.

NLC President, Mr Joe Ajaero, made the demand in a statement issued on Monday in Abuja, while calling for accountability and justice over the deaths.

Ajaero said the victims were arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining in Niger on Sept. 15 and 16.

He said the arrests occurred in the M.I. Wushishi and Lukoto areas of Niger, while the deaths were recorded on Sept. 17.

“Reports indicate that many of those who died were young people, including minors,” Ajaero said.

He said the Federal Government had constituted an independent committee to establish the identities of the deceased and determine the circumstances surrounding their deaths.

“The committee is expected to establish the identities of the deceased, circumstances of their arrest and detention, and the cause of their deaths,” he said.

Ajaero welcomed the suspension of officers connected with the incident but stressed that the measure must not replace accountability and justice.

He said the NLC mourned the victims and commiserated with the Government and people of Niger over the deaths.

The NLC president attributed participation in artisanal mining and other vulnerable informal activities to poverty, unemployment, deprivation and lack of decent livelihood opportunities.

“These were children and young people from working-class and peasant families, particularly families whose livelihoods depend on the informal economy,” Ajaero said.

He called for stronger regulation of artisanal and small-scale mining, enforcement of occupational safety standards and prohibition of hazardous child labour.

Ajaero also urged government to remove children from hazardous mining activities and provide affected families with education, skills development, social protection and alternative livelihoods.

He called for measures to address rural poverty, youth unemployment, lack of decent work and inadequate social protection.

“We cannot continue to address the symptoms of these problems while ignoring their underlying causes.”

World.title: Full list: Countries exempt from UK Student visa proof of funds
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

The UK has listed 63 countries and territories whose citizens do not have to prove they have enough money to support themselves when applying for a Student visa, under the UK’s “differential evidence requirement”.

The exemption applies to the financial requirement for living costs, according to the UK government’s official Student visa guidance. Applicants must still meet the other requirements for the visa, including having enough money to pay for their course where applicable.

The UK government said applicants from the listed countries and territories may still be asked to provide financial evidence before a decision is made on their application.

If evidence is required, UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) will contact the applicant after the application has been submitted. According to the UK government, the countries and territories covered by the differential evidence requirement are:

Australia Austria Bahrain Barbados Belgium Botswana Brazil Brunei Bulgaria Cambodia Canada Chile China Croatia Republic of Cyprus Czechia Denmark Dominican Republic Estonia Finland France Germany Greece Hong Kong Hungary Iceland Indonesia Ireland Italy Japan Kazakhstan Kuwait Latvia Liechtenstein Lithuania Luxembourg Macao Malaysia Malta Mauritius Mexico Netherlands New Zealand Norway Oman Peru Poland Portugal Qatar Romania Serbia Singapore Slovakia Slovenia South Korea Spain Sweden Switzerland Taiwan Thailand Tunisia United Arab Emirates United States of America

The UK guidance also includes British nationals overseas among those who do not need to prove they have enough money to support themselves under this provision.

How much money do other Student visa applicants need?

Applicants who are required to meet the financial requirement must generally show that they have enough money to support themselves in the UK.

For courses in London, the requirement is £1,529 per month for up to nine months while for courses outside London, the requirement is £1,171 per month for up to nine months.

The money must generally have been held for at least 28 consecutive days, with the end of that 28-day period falling within 31 days of the visa application date.

Students may also need to show enough money to pay their course fees for one academic year, up to nine months. The amount is stated on their Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS).

There are other circumstances in which an applicant does not have to prove the financial requirement.

These include applicants who have been living in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months before applying for a Student visa, and those applying as student union sabbatical officers.

Vanguard News

World.title: FG has no immediate plan to hike electricity tariff – Tegbe
World.content:
Tegbe

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Federal Government has no immediate plan to increase electricity tariffs, Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Tegbe, said on Monday, dismissing rumours of an impending hike in electricity rates across the country.

Tegbe, who spoke in Abuja while presenting his scorecard for his first 100 days in office, said electricity generation and transmission had exceeded 5,000 megawatts (MW) in recent weeks, compared with between 3,700MW and 4,700MW before June 2026.

He disclosed that the sector recorded a generation peak of 5,330MW in August and September, following interventions to restore power infrastructure and improve the performance of existing assets.

The Minister, however, acknowledged that the improvements had yet to translate into reliable electricity supply for many Nigerians, saying the immediate task was to sustain the gains and extend them to more communities.

Speaking on his performance between June 8 and September 16, 2026, Tegbe said the administration had focused on stabilising the electricity value chain, restoring market discipline and strengthening governance.

He said: “Operational record reports show generation and transmission above 5,000MW over the past couple of weeks, compared to the 3,700 to 4,700MW range before June, and a generation peak of 5,330MW during August and September.

“Our next task is to sustain these gains and translate them into more dependable supply at customer level.”

The Minister said the 375MW Alaoji open-cycle power plant, which had been offline for three years, was restored to the national grid during the period.

He also disclosed that the commissioning of new transformers at Apapa, Ijora, Alausa and Lekki in Lagos had unlocked 672MW of transmission capacity.

Similarly, a new 300-megavolt-ampere (MVA) transformer energised at Katampe, Abuja, unlocked an additional 240MW of transmission capacity.

According to him, the interventions were aimed at recovering stranded capacity and strengthening electricity delivery to major centres of demand.

Tegbe said the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had also secured the release of more than 300 containers of critical power equipment held up at the ports.

He said the equipment would be inspected, deployed and installed to support ongoing transmission infrastructure upgrades.

On electricity access, the minister said 62 solar and mini-grid installations had been completed across 30 states, providing about 43.6MW of installed solar capacity and 41,735 new connections.

The projects, he said, had an estimated beneficiary reach of more than 208,000 people.

He listed initiatives under the Rural Electrification Agency, including the 3MW solar hybrid system recently commissioned at Yakubu Gowon University, Abuja, as part of efforts to provide more dependable electricity to educational institutions.

Other projects include a 20MW off-grid initiative in Kogi State, a 3.5MW solar project in Kebbi State, a 5.5MW mini-grid in Epe, Lagos, and 39 mini-grids in Adamawa State designed to provide nearly 27MW of electricity.

The Minister said the Renewable Asset Management Company (RAMCO) would manage publicly financed renewable energy infrastructure and mobilise N3 trillion over the coming years.

On the financial health of the sector, Tegbe said the government had raised an estimated N1.23 trillion towards settling outstanding power-sector debts as part of a broader programme to address N3.3 trillion in liabilities.

He said the initiative was expected to improve liquidity across the electricity value chain and strengthen operators’ capacity to maintain infrastructure and meet their obligations.

The Minister also disclosed that the government had blocked revenue leakages associated with energy theft and other losses along the Ikorodu-Sagamu industrial corridor, estimated at approximately N120 billion annually.

He said improved billing, collection and remittance would help preserve resources needed to sustain electricity supply.

On metering, Tegbe said approximately 350,000 meters were installed during his first 100 days in office, bringing cumulative installations to 1,004,260 as of August 2026.

He added that the resolution of the AMMON litigation had unlocked the procurement of about 1.4 million smart meters across affected programmes.

The Minister said metering of military formations was also progressing, with 90,000 installations recorded, while 5,000 young Nigerians were undergoing training as smart-meter installers under the Power Force programme.

Tegbe reiterated that the government had no immediate plan to increase electricity tariffs.

He said the next phase of the reform programme would focus on stabilising key transmission corridors, including Lagos, Enugu-Port Harcourt and Abuja-Kaduna-Kano, while advancing the proposed Transmission Super Grid.

The Minister said technical audits had commenced along the Lagos and Abuja corridors to identify weak points and guide investments towards interventions with measurable system impact.

He added that the government would also pursue bilateral arrangements between generation and distribution companies to improve capacity utilisation and payment certainty.

On future investments, Tegbe said engagements with Chinese companies had secured commitments to accelerate priority power projects, including the 1.9-gigawatt Presidential Power Initiative, with the first transmission lines scheduled for delivery in the first quarter of 2027.

He said the government would continue efforts to strengthen grid protection and control systems, improve gas availability to power plants, and address vandalism and electricity theft.

Acknowledging that the national generation peak did not necessarily reflect the electricity experience of every community, Tegbe said the government would measure progress through supply reliability, billing accuracy, and the resolution of faults and complaints.

He said the government would work over the next six months to translate the repairs and reforms into more visible improvements in electricity supply.

World.title: Tinubu’s vacation: Who is in charge of Nigeria? Atiku asks
World.content:
Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has questioned who is constitutionally exercising presidential authority in Nigeria following the expiration of the three-week vacation announced for President Bola Tinubu.

Tinubu left Nigeria on August 30 for what the Presidency described as a three-week working vacation in Europe.

The Presidency said on Monday that the President had extended his stay by a few days and would return to Nigeria at the weekend.

In a statement titled “Who is in Charge of Nigeria?”, Atiku cited Section 145 of the 1999 Constitution, which provides for the President to transmit a written declaration to the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House when proceeding on vacation, allowing the Vice President to perform presidential functions as Acting President.

He said Nigerians had not been shown any such communication transferring presidential authority to Vice President Kashim Shettima.

“Twenty-one days have come and gone since President Bola Ahmed Tinubu left Nigeria on what the Presidency described as a three-week annual vacation,” Atiku said.

“Today, Nigerians are entitled to ask a very simple constitutional question: Who is in charge of Nigeria?”

According to Atiku, if the required declaration was not transmitted within 21 days, Section 145(2) provides for the National Assembly to mandate the Vice President to perform the functions of President as Acting President.

He therefore challenged the Presidency to publish the letter if it exists and asked the National Assembly to explain why the constitutional procedure had not been activated if no declaration was transmitted.

“If such a letter exists, the Presidency should publish it immediately,” he said.

The ADC candidate also raised concerns over the simultaneous absence of Tinubu and Shettima, with the Vice President in New York representing Nigeria at the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

“So again: who is exercising presidential authority in Nigeria today, and under what constitutional instrument?” Atiku asked.

He described the matter as one of “constitutional order” rather than political convenience, adding that Nigeria could not be governed through informal arrangements.

“Nigeria cannot be governed by assumptions. It cannot be governed by presidential social-media posts from Europe.

“It cannot be governed by photographs from private dinners at the Élysée Palace.

“It cannot be governed on autopilot,” he said.

Atiku also cited the deaths of 37 Nigerians in NSCDC custody in Minna and rising petrol prices, which he said had added to the economic difficulties facing Nigerians.

“These are not ordinary times. Yet the President is abroad. The Vice President is abroad. The Senate President is abroad,” he said.

He called on the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House to confirm whether they received any communication from Tinubu under Section 145(1).

Atiku added: “Nigeria is bigger than any President. At a time of severe economic hardship, rising energy costs, security challenges and the shocking deaths of citizens in government custody, the country deserves visible, accountable and constitutionally grounded leadership.”

“The question will not disappear: Who, constitutionally, is in charge of Nigeria?”

World.title: Plateau Declares Dusk‑to‑Dawn Curfew in Barkin Ladi, Bokkos, Mangu
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The Plateau State Government has announced an immediate dusk‑to‑dawn curfew across Barkin Ladi, Bokkos and Mangu Local Government Areas following emerging security threats that officials say require urgent containment.

The directive, effective Monday, restricts movement between 6:00 PM and 6:00 AM until further notice. Government sources describe the measure as a necessary intervention to stabilize the affected communities and prevent a further breakdown of law and order.

In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Communication, Rt. Hon. Joyce Lohya Ramnap, the administration of Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang said the curfew was part of a coordinated security response aimed at protecting lives and restoring calm.

According to the statement, residents in the three local government areas are expected to comply fully with the directive and adjust their commercial, agricultural and personal activities to fit within the permitted hours.

The government emphasized that the restriction is designed to minimize hardship while ensuring that security agencies can operate effectively.

Security operatives have been ordered to enforce the curfew strictly, including an immediate ban on the use of motorcycles within the affected areas. Authorities, however, assured citizens that enforcement will be carried out professionally and with respect for human rights.

The government urged residents to remain vigilant, cooperate with security personnel and report suspicious activities as efforts continue to restore normalcy.

World.title: 2027: Fresh Crisis Rocks NDC Over Plateau Guber Substitution Primary
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The crisis rocking the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Plateau State has assumed a different dimension following allegations that the party’s state chairman, Solomon Yakub, sent a strange name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as the purported winner of the substitution governorship election held last Tuesday.

However, Yakubu denied any wrong doing, saying that he was not aware of any contention following the emergence of the winner of Plateau State governorship ticket of NDC, stressing that INEC monitored the exercise and compiled their report.

The National Auditor of NDC, Oluwole Adedapo, who was delegated by the party’s National Working Committee (NWC) to conduct the exercise, declared that Da Jonathan Akuns was returned unopposed.

Adedapo, while announcing the result of the substitution primary, disclosed that on arrival in Jos, he paid a courtesy visit to the party’s state Exco at the state secretariat where he explained the purpose of his mission

He expressed surprise that at about 10.30pm on the eve of the substitution primary, some persons who claimed to be operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) stormed the venue, urging him to follow them to their office.

Adedapo explained that going by the NDC records, only Akuns purchased the expression of interest and nomination forms of the party and was successfully screened, stressing that the idea of the substitution primary was to receive stakeholder affirmation since there was no challenger.

He said: “The party faithful present at the meeting refused the invitation and informed the DSS officers that Adedapo was sent from Abuja and that this was a political family meeting and not an illegal assembly.

“The next day, which was Tuesday, the date of the primary proper, the state chairman shouted at me and attempted to disrupt the exercise.

“He dragged chairmen of seven LGAs to go and hold an illegal parallel exercise. The responsibility of conducting the governorship primary is that of the national leadership of the party.”

But, a stakeholder, Abdullahi Iliya, told journalists that after holding a parallel substitution primary with NDC chairmen of seven local government areas, Yakubu sent the name of Alfred Damiyal, a defeated governorship aspirant from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) gubernatorial primary, to the INEC.

He noted that in the bid to perfect his breach of due process, Yakubu passed the report of his parallel exercise through the Plateau State office of the Election and Party Monitoring (EPM) unit for onward transmission to the INEC headquarters.

When contacted, the NDC National Secretary, Ikenna Enekweizu, said that the NDC had forwarded to INEC the name of Akuns, its nominee for the Plateau State governorship 2027 poll.

He stressed that it would be strange for INEC to accept any communication that was not endorsed by the national chairman and secretary, stressing that it was a settled tradition that only the national leadership of a political party should organise party primaries and forward to INEC the list of nominated candidates.

Enekweizu noted: “I heard that the Plateau State chairman sent a name to INEC, but I am just hearing the suggestion that my signature and that of the national chairman could have been cloned. If INEC accepted the letter from the state chairman, we would challenge them to show us the letter if they acted on any names contrary to what we sent to them.

“We have forwarded the name of Da Jonathan Sunday Akuns to INEC and anything outside that is an aberration.”

World.title: Academic Activities Return to Fedpoly Offa After Crisis of Confidence Between ASUP, Mgt.
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Academic activities were on Monday restored to the Federal Polytechnic (Fedpoly), Offa, Kwara State after crisis of confidence between the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP) and the school management.

Already, the suspended semester examinations of the institution also commenced Monday on the two campuses.

ASUP had September 15, 2026 withdrew its services pending the restoration of alleged security concerns raised by the institution.

There has been a misunderstanding between the school authorities and ASUP over holding of council’s meetings outside the polytechnic campuses for alleged insecurity.

ASUP specifically accused the management of misinforming the Federal Ministry of Education to justify holding of its meetings outside the polytechnic.

ASUP, in a letter to the Chairman, Governing Council, Federal Polytechnic Offa, Kwara State signed by its Chairman, Yemi Alabi, said members withdrew their services since September 15, 2026 as a result of alleged security concerns as raised by the institution.

The letter entitled: ‘RE: Holding of governing council meetings outside the polytechnic,’ read: “It is no news that our institution has been plagued with unprecedented industrial disharmony over the year and this instability has been reiterated by the union to be hinged on poor working conditions, declining staff welfare, uninhabitable working environment etal.

“But the council has turned a blind eye on these palpable concerns.”

Alabi alleged that the council had justified alleged insecurity as the reason for the shift of council meetings to Ilorin, the state capital, adding that during a meeting on September 12, this year council recapitulated.

Alabi added: “On the strength of the above, the union is compelled to conclude that the governing council has failed entirely in their oversight functions; that the rector and the governing council have conducted themselves in ways capable of tampering with the peace of the institution and host community; that the governing council/rector have misinformed the Federal Ministry of Education and channelled them towards an administrative error; that the institution is no longer safe for staffers.

“Consequently, the union is hereby calling for the immediate suspension of.the Rector, Engr. Kamoru Kadiri, for alleged sundry malfeasance, while also giving a vote of no confidence on the principal officers and governing council.

“This correspondence is also a formal communication if the immediate and withdrawal of services.of academic staff till we have a remedy to security concerns by the ministry of education.”

Approving the request, Director (Polytechnic Education and Allied Institutions) on behalf of the Minister of Education, Mrs Igwe Amy K, said that the meetings be conducted with strict adherence to due process.

Mrs Igwe said: “I am directed to convey you the approval of the Hon Minister, for the Governing Council and Council’s statutory committee’s meetings to be convened at temporarily suitable venues outside the confines of the polytechnic due to security reasons, as you requested.”

Speaking with journalists in Ilorin Monday on the state of the polytechnic, the Rector, Kadir, said that normal academic activities are now ongoing at the institution after a few days of disruption.

“As I am talking to you our semester exams are ongoing. As par the allegation of holding meetings outside the premises of the school, council sought approval from the Education Minister,” the rectory said.

Kadiri, in a letter on behalf of the governing council of the school to education minister in August this year, obtained by THISDAY, claimed that: “The decision to hold council and committee meetings outside the polytechnic should not be construed as a departure from the statutory responsibilities of the governing council or a definition of the authority of the polytechnic.

“Rather, it is a temporary and precautionary administrative measure adopted in the overriding interest of institutional stability, effective governance, personal security and the uninterrupted discharge of the council’s statutory functions.”

Kadir therefore urged the union to allow peace reign supreme so as to advance the academic excellence of the institution.

World.title: Obi’s Camp Tackles Alake Over 37 Deaths in Niger
World.content:
* Says Solid Minerals minister should explain tragedy before attacking Obi

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Peter Obi Media Office has faulted the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, for engaging in political exchanges over Peter Obi’s record as Anambra State governor, while questions remain unanswered over the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State.

The media office, in a statement issued on Monday by its spokesman, Idris Zekeri Jnr, described Alake’s comments on Obi’s administration in Anambra as a distraction from the tragedy in the solid minerals sector.

The statement followed remarks by Alake, who, while speaking in his capacity as a spokesperson of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, said Obi had “nowhere to hide” over what he described as the former governor’s poor record in Anambra State.

The Obi Media Office said the minister should instead concentrate on providing answers to questions surrounding the deaths of the 37 detainees, whose circumstances have triggered public outrage, protests and calls for an independent investigation.

Part of the statement read: “Instead of fixing the catastrophic failures in Nigeria’s solid minerals sector, providing answers to these questions: Who authorised the operation?

“What safeguards were in place? Who failed? And who will be held accountable? A minister overseeing a sector at the centre of such a tragic episode is busy trying to create a distraction.”

The deaths occurred after the suspects were arrested during operations against alleged illegal mining in Niger State on September 15 and 16.

The Federal Government has suspended officials and constituted a 10-member committee to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths, while police authorities have also opened an investigation.

The exact cause of death remains under investigation. Initial accounts attributed the deaths to a possible disease outbreak, while survivors and other stakeholders have alleged that overcrowding and poor ventilation contributed to suffocation.

The Obi Media Office said the tragedy should compel the government to focus on accountability and reforms rather than political exchanges.

“For us in Peter Obi Media, there is a tragic irony in watching high-ranking public officials prioritise political posturing over executive accountability,” the office said.

It added that the deaths represented more than statistics, stressing that the victims were Nigerians who had died while in government custody after being arrested in connection with alleged illegal mining.

The statement urged the Federal Government to strengthen regulation of the mining industry and address illegal and unsafe mining operations.

“Ending unchecked illegal operations and curbing informal and unregulated extraction that endangers vulnerable youth seeking a livelihood is the minister’s responsibility,” it said.

The media office further argued that young Nigerians deserved a mining sector founded on safety, regulation and sustainable development, rather than one in which political arguments took precedence over questions of public accountability.

The statement also accused the APC administration of failing Nigerians across various sectors, but provided no specific evidence for the broader claim.

The renewed political exchange followed an attack by the APC Presidential Campaign Council on Obi over his record as Anambra governor, particularly allegations concerning the state’s debt position when he left office in 2014.

The campaign council has urged Obi to withdraw from the 2027 presidential race.

Alake, in his statement, relied on figures presented by the Anambra State Government concerning external borrowing and expenditure during Obi’s tenure.

According to the figures cited by Alake, Obi’s administration contracted about $123.77 million in external loans, while subsequent administrations continued to service the obligations.

The Obi Media Office, however, maintained that Alake should give priority to the solid minerals portfolio under his supervision.

It said the circumstances surrounding the Niger deaths demanded “sober reflection and immediate systemic reform”, insisting that accountability should be established through the ongoing investigations.

The office urged the government to end illegal mining, improve safety standards and protect young Nigerians involved in artisanal mining.

“Nigerian youths deserve a solid minerals sector built on safety, regulation and sustainable development and not an executive office that chases political shadows while tragedy unfolds on its watch,” it said.

World.title: AI‑Driven Disinformation Threatens Nigeria’s Security Operations, Expert Warns
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

Artificial intelligence–powered disinformation, deepfakes and coordinated online propaganda pose a growing threat to Nigeria’s security architecture and public trust, technology and media expert Job Mwadkon Dachungyang has cautioned.

Delivering a keynote address at a media workshop organised by the Directorate of Army Public Relations (DAPR) for Army public relations officers, media practitioners and communication personnel from other security agencies, Dachungyang said modern security operations now unfold on two battlefields; the physical environment and the fast‑moving digital information space.

He noted that the widespread use of smartphones and social media means information about security incidents often reaches millions before authorities verify the facts. This speed, he said, complicates joint operations involving multiple agencies with different communication structures.

Dachungyang explained that while artificial intelligence offers opportunities for real‑time sentiment analysis, threat monitoring and early crisis detection, it also introduces new vulnerabilities. He warned that AI‑generated fake videos, audio recordings and official‑looking messages could mislead the public, disrupt operations or imitate senior commanders to circulate false instructions.

He described deepfakes as a particularly dangerous tool, noting that fabricated content could trigger panic or confusion among security personnel and civilians.

The technology expert also identified delays in official communication as a major weakness. When verified information is not released quickly, he said, rumours and speculation fill the gap. He urged security institutions to adopt faster verification and communication systems capable of matching the speed of online misinformation.

Dachungyang further highlighted communication silos among the military, police, intelligence agencies and other security institutions. Conflicting statements, he said, can undermine otherwise successful operations and erode public confidence. He argued that media and public relations must be integrated into operational planning from the start, not treated as an administrative afterthought.

According to him, public trust is now a core element of national security. Communities are more likely to cooperate with security agencies when institutions demonstrate credibility, consistency, clarity, speed and transparency. Stronger trust, he added, improves the flow of information from citizens to security agencies, especially in areas affected by insecurity.

To counter emerging digital threats, Dachungyang recommended the establishment of AI verification and fact‑checking units capable of detecting deepfakes, investigating coordinated online manipulation and verifying digital content. He also proposed multi‑agency media intelligence frameworks to ensure real‑time coordination during joint operations.

He called for deeper collaboration between security institutions, media organisations and judicial authorities to tackle malicious disinformation and digital manipulation.

Dachungyang said the evolving information landscape requires security leaders and public relations officers to adopt a new three‑part leadership model: battle‑ready, media‑ready and AI‑aware. This, he said, demands an understanding of tactical operations, crisis communication, digital verification and the influence of AI‑driven platforms on public narratives.

The workshop aligns with the Nigerian Army’s ongoing efforts to strengthen media engagement, sustain public support for operations and communicate successes across various theatres.

World.title: Ugandan Lawmakers Seek Nigeria’s Expertise on Sustainable Borrowing, Public Funds
World.content:
* NILDS DG urges scrutiny of loans, debt, guarantees

* As Uganda targets 6.5–7% growth in 2026

…Lawmakers say Africa must learn from its own successes, mistakes rather than rely on Europe

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Members of Uganda’s Parliamentary Committee on National Economy have arrived in Nigeria to deepen their capacity to scrutinise government borrowing, loan guarantees and public expenditure, with the delegation saying Nigeria’s democratic experience offers valuable lessons for African countries.

The Ugandan lawmakers made the disclosure on Monday in Abuja at the opening of a five-day training and induction workshop organised by the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS) for members and technical staff of the Committee on National Economy of the Parliament of Uganda.

Speaking at the event, the Team Lead of the Ugandan delegation, Hon. Avur Jane Pacuto, said the lawmakers deliberately chose Nigeria as a destination for parliamentary learning because of what she described as the country’s growing democratic experience.

Pacuto, a three-term member of the Ugandan Parliament, said African countries should increasingly draw lessons from one another instead of depending exclusively on experiences from Europe.

She said: “We are here today as leaders from Uganda to learn and share from you, being a sister country in the Commonwealth.

“Because Nigeria is increasingly becoming very democratic, we thought there was no better place than Nigeria to come to.”

She said the delegation was particularly interested in learning how governments could manage borrowing responsibly and ensure that borrowed resources were deployed for the benefit of citizens.

According to her, Uganda’s Committee on National Economy has the responsibility of reviewing, assessing and scrutinising government borrowing, grants and guarantees, making the training particularly relevant to its parliamentary mandate.

“We are here to learn more about how borrowed resources should be used for the common good of our citizens, being cognisant of the fact that there are times where there are wastages and leakages in public funds,” Pacuto said.

The Ugandan lawmaker said the committee also sought to understand how African governments could borrow sustainably amid changing global economic conditions, particularly fluctuations in exchange rates.

She explained that the visit was not the first time Ugandan parliamentarians had participated in programmes at NILDS, adding that the delegation expected to gain fresh insights into Nigeria’s economic management and institutional practices.

Pacuto said the lawmakers were also interested in Nigeria’s cultural diversity and other areas of institutional experience, while inviting Nigerian legislators and NILDS officials to Uganda for further engagements and experience-sharing.

Earlier, the NILDS Director-General, Prof. Abubakar Sulaiman, said effective parliamentary performance went beyond lawmaking to include rigorous oversight, public finance scrutiny and accountability in the management of national resources.

Sulaiman said Uganda’s projected economic growth of between 6.5 and seven per cent in 2026 offered encouraging prospects but cautioned that economic expansion alone could not guarantee inclusive and sustainable development.

He identified sound public financial management, fiscal discipline, debt sustainability, efficient public expenditure and productive development investments as critical determinants of whether economic growth would translate into improved welfare for citizens.

The NILDS DG said the Committee on National Economy occupied a strategic position in Uganda’s economic governance framework because of its responsibilities for scrutinising national loans and loan guarantees, public financial aggregates, government debt and strategies for improving the national economy.

He urged the lawmakers and their technical advisers to go beyond examining figures contained in loan proposals and interrogate the purpose, cost, expected returns and sustainability of government borrowing.

Sulaiman said legislators should determine whether loan-financed projects were delivering the outcomes for which they were approved and whether borrowed resources were advancing Uganda’s long-term development priorities.

“Questions surrounding sovereign borrowing, debt sustainability, loan guarantees and externally financed projects involve complex economic, financial and legal considerations,” he said.

He stressed that parliamentary oversight should be driven by evidence, rather than either automatic opposition to government proposals or uncritical approval of them.

“Effective oversight is about asking the right questions, demanding credible evidence, identifying risks, assessing alternatives and ensuring that public resources are deployed in accordance with the national interest,” Sulaiman said.

He said the rapidly changing global environment had made continuous parliamentary capacity development increasingly important, citing geopolitical tensions, changing patterns of global trade and investment, technological disruption, climate-related vulnerabilities, commodity-price fluctuations and evolving international financial conditions.

The NILDS boss also highlighted the African Continental Free Trade Area and efforts to strengthen regional economic integration as developments requiring African legislatures to build stronger institutional and technical capacity.

According to him, African economies must develop resilience against external shocks while positioning themselves to take advantage of emerging opportunities.

Sulaiman said modern parliaments needed legislators and technical staff capable of analysing complex economic data, fiscal projections, debt instruments, public expenditure frameworks and development-financing arrangements.

He therefore called for continuous training and retraining of parliamentary professionals, noting that economic conditions, government policies, financial instruments and sources of public financing were constantly changing.

The NILDS DG said the institute’s engagement with the Ugandan Parliament was not intended to present Nigeria’s experience as a model to be copied wholesale.

Rather, he said, the programme was designed to facilitate comparative learning, critical reflection and the adaptation of useful practices to Uganda’s institutional and national circumstances.

He listed the expected outcomes of the training to include stronger capacity to analyse macroeconomic and fiscal developments, and scrutinising sovereign borrowing and loan guarantees.

He also listed other benefits to include assessment of debt sustainability, monitor externally financed projects, review fiscal responsibility and budget performance, conduct evidence-based oversight and produce stronger committee reports and recommendations.

Sulaiman added that Nigeria and Uganda, despite operating in different economic and institutional environments, shared common challenges relating to fiscal sustainability, public borrowing, debt management, revenue mobilisation, budget implementation and parliamentary oversight.

He said the workshop would therefore strengthen cooperation between the two countries and contribute to improved legislative oversight of public resources.

Sulaiman said Uganda’s growth prospects could only be sustained through prudent economic policies, responsible borrowing, productive investment and strong institutions of accountability.

“A Parliament that learns continuously is better positioned to legislate effectively, oversee responsibly and represent its citizens meaningfully,” he said.

World.title: Presidency: Tinubu’s Working Leave Has Been Extended By One Week
World.content:
.Says President’ll continue to ask VP Shettima and SGF Akume to represent him at functions

.Describes Atiku’s insinuation about Tinubu’s absence at UNGA as baseless and irresponsible

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Monday disclosed that the three-week working leave embarked upon by President Bola Tinubu has been extended by one week.

Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga in a release stated that the President will return to Nigeria at the weekend, following the extension of his working vacation by a few days.

Tinubu departed Nigeria on August 30 for London to begin the working vacation.

According to the Presidency, the President after spending a week in London, he moved to Paris, France, where he met with French President Emmanuel Macron and businessman Mr Vincent Bollore, whose media group includes Canal+, Multichoice, and Universal Music Group.

Since he began the vacation, Tinubu has continued to keep in touch with home, directing the affairs of the nation, like ordering an independent panel to investigate the death of 37 illegal miners in Minna, following their detention by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, among other things.

While away, the President delegated Vice President Kashim Shettima to represent him at some official functions. Though Shettima left Abuja on October 20 for New York to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, who has also been representing the President at events, will continue to do so.

On the political front, the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abubakar Yari, has been leading notable party leaders in consultations with prominent traditional rulers in the country.

The Presidency described the baseless insinuation by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and a United States-based lobbying firm headed by an ex-convict about President Tinubu’s non-attendance at UNGA as irresponsible.

Vice President Shettima, who is representing the President at the global conference, will present Nigeria’s national statement.

World.title: Be Fearless, Decisive Against Terrorists, Theatre Commander Charges 925 Forest Guards
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Theatre Commander of Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), Major General Ibikunle Ajose, has charged 925 newly trained Borno State Forest Guards to remain fearless, decisive and professional as they support ongoing efforts to counter terrorism and other criminal activities across the state.

Major General Ajose gave the charge at the graduation ceremony of the Forest Guards following their two-week in-theatre acclimatisation training at the North-East Theatre Training School (NETTS), Buni Yadi, Yobe State, on 20 September 2026.

Addressing the graduates, the Theatre Commander said their training and knowledge of the local terrain would complement ongoing military operations and enhance the effectiveness of counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency efforts.

According to a statement by the Acting Military Information Officer of Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, the Commander urged the Forest Guards to apply their newly acquired skills responsibly, remain disciplined and respect law-abiding citizens, while warning against the harassment of civilians and rivalry with other security agencies.

He charged them to remain focused on the common threat posed by terrorists and criminals and to demonstrate courage and decisiveness in the discharge of their duties.

The Special Guest of Honour, the Executive Governor of Borno State, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, represented by the Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar, stated that the Forest Guard initiative was established to provide structured auxiliary support to the Armed Forces and other security agencies.

He disclosed that the 925 personnel, drawn from the 27 Local Government Areas of Borno State, would be handed over to the Theatre Command for deployment based on operational requirements.

He noted that their knowledge of the local terrain, languages and culture would enhance their effectiveness as force multipliers in support of ongoing operations.

Earlier, the Commandant of NETTS, Brigadier General Amadike Onaogu, explained that the two-week training was designed to build the confidence, resilience, discipline and adaptability required of the Forest Guards in their supporting role.

He emphasised that the training was not intended to transform them into soldiers, but to equip them with relevant competencies to effectively complement ongoing security operations within their areas of responsibility.

Major General Ajose commended the Borno State Government for its sustained support for security efforts in the state and appreciated the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, for his continued guidance and support for Operation Hadin Kai and the training programme.

He also commended the Commandant and instructors of NETTS for maintaining the required training standards and urged them to sustain the tempo.

The Theatre Commander further charged the newly graduated Forest Guards to uphold discipline, professionalism and respect for the law as they commence their duties.

He reaffirmed OPHK’s commitment to sustaining operational pressure against terrorists while deepening cooperation with relevant security stakeholders towards restoring lasting peace and normalcy across the Theatre of Operations.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs made a mistake by releasing Cele, says club legend
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs midfielder Willard Katsanda believes Amakhosi made a mistake by releasing Thabo Cele.

The 28-year-old midfield maestro joined Chiefs in January 2025 but only spent 18 months at the club before he was let go a few weeks ago.

Mamelodi Sundowns were quick to pounce on Cele and Katsanda feels his former club lost a quality player.



“Personally, I thought he was brilliant for us. I liked his game a lot, to be honest. He is a top-quality midfielder, there is no doubt about that,” Katsande told FARPost.

Chiefs release Cele, Sundowns pounce

With Cele gone, Amakhosi signed Adolf Mtaswinga but the Tanzanian is yet to make his mark after struggling to adjust to South African football.

Katsande feels Chiefs had time to review their decision about Cele during pre-season.

“But football is like that. At the end of the season, the club has to sit down, review, and decide which direction they want to go.

“Once that decision is made, these things can happen,” he said.

Amakhosi have drawn four of their last games and only picked up seven from a possible 15 points. Their goalless draw against Golden Arrows sees them seven points behind log leaders Mamelodi Sundowns.



Cele’s departure at Chiefs could affect them in the coming weeks if a midfield player gets injured. Lebohang Maboe, who has been Amakhosi’s best player, was subbed off against Arrows this past weekend but the injury appear not be be serious.

Do you think Amakhosi should have kept Cele?

World.title: Dawn Park murder: Two women charged in love-triangle twist
World.content:
Two women accused in the Jabulile Ntimba murder case during proceedings at the Boksburg Magistrates’ Court. The pair face murder and other charges linked to the Dawn Park killing. Image: SABC

Two women accused of murdering Jabulile Ntimba in Dawn Park have appeared in the Boksburg Magistrates’ Court, where the State revealed an alleged relationship dispute at the centre of the case.

Fortunate Masilela, 31, and Tsakane Msithani, 38, face charges of murder, defeating the ends of justice and possession of a dangerous weapon.

The case relates to Ntimba’s murder in Dawn Park on 16 September 2026.



The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) said Masilela and Msithani knew Ntimba and were allegedly with her on the night she died.

Police later found Ntimba dead and launched an investigation that led to the arrests of the two women.

Investigators also recovered items believed to be relevant to the case.

State reveals alleged relationship dispute

The State alleges that Ntimba was in a relationship with Masilela’s husband, who was also allegedly Ntimba’s boyfriend.

The man is also Msithani’s brother.

According to the NPA, the discovery of the alleged relationship preceded Ntimba’s murder.



The allegations have not yet been tested in court.

Police previously said investigators were examining whether Ntimba’s killing stemmed from a relationship-related matter, including what authorities described as a possible love triangle.

Third suspect not charged

Police initially arrested a third person as investigators followed leads in the case.

However, the State decided not to place the matter against that person on the court roll because prosecutors said there was insufficient evidence at this stage.

The investigation remains open.

State to oppose bail

The Boksburg Magistrates’ Court postponed the matter to 1 October 2026 for a formal bail application.

The State will oppose bail.

Masilela and Msithani will remain in custody until their next court appearance.

NPA Gauteng communications officer Magaboke Mohlatlole said prosecutors would continue working with SAPS to ensure investigators place all relevant evidence before the court.

World.title: What Thabo Senong and Yeye have changed at Zimbabwean club
World.content:
Something has changed at FC Platinum since South Africans Thabo Senong and Reneilwe “Yeye” Letsholonyane took charge.

The Zimbabwean PSL side are beginning to look more organised, difficult to break down and, most importantly, consistent.

Senong was appointed FC Platinum head coach in July, replacing Joel Luphahla, while former Kaizer Chiefs and Bafana Bafana midfielder Letsholonyane joined him as his assistant.



The pair had to wait more than three weeks for their work permits before officially taking charge.

But since they took charge, the results started to change.

FC Platinum: Four games, no goals conceded

FC Platinum’s recent run under the South African coaching duo has been particularly impressive defensively.

They beat Agama 1-0 on Senong’s debut, defeated Blackrock 2-0 in the ZIFA Munhumutapa Challenge Cup, held Scottland to a 0-0 draw and then edged ZPC Kariba 1-0.

The latest victory made it three wins for Senong.

That means five goals scored and none conceded across the four matches.



The clean sheet against Scottland was especially significant, considering the strength of the league leaders.

It suggests that Senong and Letsholonyane have quickly placed an emphasis on organisation and discipline without completely sacrificing their attacking approach.

FC Platinum coach wants more from his attack

Despite the defensive improvement, Senong knows there is still work to do.

Ahead of the ZPC Kariba match, the coach said the team had worked on physical and tactical aspects both individually and collectively.

He also identified FC Platinum’s efficiency in the final third as an area that needed improvement.

That could be the next step in the South African coach’s project.

FC Platinum have become difficult to score against, but turning those strong defensive performances into more goals will be important as the season enters its final stages.

Yeye’s experience adds another dimension

Letsholonyane is also bringing his own coaching experience to the project.

The 44-year-old spent last season as head coach of Botswana Premier League side Matebele FC, helping the club retain its top-flight status and earning a Coach of the Season nomination.

He has described his move to Zimbabwe as an opportunity to gain international experience and continue developing as a coach.

For FC Platinum, the partnership is still in its early stages.

But four matches have already provided a clear indication of what Senong and Yeye are trying to build.

World.title: Cape Town’s dam levels after the recent blast of rain
World.content:
Voëlvlei Dam has a capacity of 164 095 million litres when full. Image: Zahid Badroodien/ Facebook

Cape Town’s dams have received a boost following recent rain across the Western Cape, with overall storage climbing to 76.6%.

The latest combined figures from the City of Cape Town show that 687 898 million litres are currently stored across the six major dams.

That’s up from 75.9% on 4 September.



However, the latest figures also highlight the gap between Cape Town’s water position now and this time last year.

The combined storage level stood at 92.3% on 21 September 2025. This year’s figure is therefore 15.7 percentage points lower.

Dam levels get a boost after rain

The City’s latest figures show increases at most of the major dams compared with the previous week. Berg River is now 94.2% full, up from 91.2%.

Steenbras Upper has also jumped from 83.6% to 95%. Theewaterskloof edged up from 76.3% to 76.8%.

Voëlvlei increased from 58.6% to 59.2%, while Wemmershoek climbed from 88.6% to 89.5%.

Steenbras Lower recorded the biggest percentage increase over the week. Its level rose from 47.7% to 50.4%.



Current Dam Water Levels for Cape Town:

Major dams Storage Ml % Capacity when full 21/9/2026 Berg River 130 010 94.2 Steenbras Lower 33 517 50.4 Steenbras Upper 31 767 95.0 Theewaterskloof 480 188 76.8 Voëlvlei 164 095 59.2 Wemmershoek 58 644 89.5 Total Stored Ml 898 221 687 898 % Storage 76.6

‘Water supply remains secure’

Cape Town has witnessed a drier-than-usual winter in 2026, while large parts of the south-western Western Cape experienced their driest July on record as the global effects of El Niño are being felt.

City officials are trying to avoid a repeat of the 2017/18 Cape Town water crisis, and the looming threat of a ‘Day Zero.’

As such, Dr Zahid Badroodien, Cape Town’s MMC for Water and Sanitation, allayed fears that Capetonians would be hit with water restrictions.

“Our city’s water supply remains secure in the immediate term,” Badroodien said on Monday. “We currently do not anticipate any water shortages.”

However, he did warn that the stored water must support a wider region through the hotter and drier summer months, until the next winter rainfall season.

The Western Cape Water Supply System also supplies other municipalities and the agricultural sector. The City says it is monitoring dam levels, rainfall and water demand.

City urges residents to use water responsibly

Badroodien said the City is continuing with pressure management, leak detection and repairs.

Other measures include pipe replacements and treated effluent use as an alternative water supply. The City is also investing in groundwater abstraction, water reuse and other diversified sources.

“Our water security is a regional responsibility,” Badroodien added. “We are engaging other municipalities as well as other users of the Western Cape water supply system to ensure a coordinated approach.”

“We continue to ask our residents and businesses to please help us reduce our water footprint and our water demand by using water responsibly.”

World.title: Male suspect in Jabulile Ntimba’s murder released
World.content:
JOAHNNESBURG - The NPA has not enrolled the case against the male suspect who had been arrested in connection with the death of the ninth Ekurhuleni victim.

However, the two women who were apprehended with him over the weekend face premeditated murder and obstruction of justice charges for Jabulile Ntimba’s death.

The duo made their first appearance in the Boksburg Magistrate’s Court.

READ | Woman's body found wrapped in duvet at Moroka Dam

The matter was postponed to 1 October for a bail application.

Authorities believe Ntimba’s death may be related to a love triangle.

The 30-year-old’s body was discovered on the side of the road in Dawn Park, Gauteng, semi-naked and wrapped in a sheet.

World.title: Maboe injury doubt for Bafana Bafana
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Bafana Bafana coach Pitso Mosimane is hopeful Lebohang Maboe can still play some part in the upcoming AFCON qualifiers.

The Kaizer Chiefs midfielder was substituted off during his side's goalless draw with Golden Arrows over the weekend.

According to Mosimane, Maboe has a 'niggling ankle'.

"The doctor has briefed me that we should be careful with him and give him a chance...He's going for a scan which will tell us how far he is..."

South Africa to host Guinea on Saturday at the Orlando Stadium in Johannesburg before travelling to Egypt to play Eritrea four days later.

World.title: Senior cop arrested for sexual grooming and rape
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A senior police officer has been arrested for allegedly raping an 18-year-old girl in a hotel in Sandton in May.

He also faces charges relating to the sexual grooming of a 16-year-old girl between July and August 2026.

Police spokesperson Athlenda Mathe said the 59-year-old officer, who holds the rank of Lieutenant General, was arrested on Monday by the members of the Commission's Recommendations Task Team (CRTT).

READ | KZN suspected serial rapist case postponed to 28 September

The officer is expected to appear before the Randburg Magistrate's Court on Tuesday.

Acting National Commissioner of the South African Police Service (SAPS), Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane welcomed the arrest.

In the same breath, she condemned the alleged conduct, which comes as the country faces mounting cases of gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF).

"Police officers are entrusted with protecting women and children. They cannot themselves be implicated in conduct that undermines this responsibility," she said.

World.title: Sibanyoni admits knowing Fanie Nkosi as social acquaintance, a mover and shaker
World.content:
PRETORIA - Taxi boss Joe Sibanyoni says he knew suspended crime intelligence officer Fannie Nkosi socially.

He told the Madlanga Commission that WhatsApp messages show that Nkosi turned to KZN Police Commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi for assistance.

Sibanyoni says Nkosi contacted Mkhwanazi for help with his meetings with Mandla Gcaba Snr., who was a mutual contact.

READ: Sibanyoni fights bail conditions

Sibanyoni has been implicated in allegations of corruption, underworld syndicates and organised crime, with links to the Big 5 Cartel.

He has told the commission he won't go into his extortion case, as it falls outside the commission's mandate.

During his first appearance before the commission, Sibanyoni was questioned about the taxi industry and alleged links to the so-called Big Five cartel.

Sibanyoni and three co-accused face charges of extortion and money laundering in connection with allegations of a protection racket in Mpumalanga.

He and his co-accused are currently out on bail.

World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Intercape CEO Johann Ferreira has detailed a culture of intimidation that threatens businesses in South Africa.

People with interests in the taxi industry are believed to be leading a campaign of violence against the transport company.

READ | Spring Day vandalism takes Tshwane buses off road

The courts have granted Intercape 16 judgments ordering the police, the Eastern Cape Transport MEC, and national government to keep the company’s staff and passengers safe.

The latest High Court judgment asserts the right of Intercape to load and offload passengers at the Ngcobo Police Station in the Eastern Cape.

World.title: 'Wherever we govern, jobs are created in numbers'- Hill-Lewis

GQEBERHA - 'Wherever we govern, jobs are created in big numbers'.

These were the words of DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis as he addressed communities in Nelson Mandela Bay.

On Monday, Hill-Lewis visited the metro as part of his party's Working for All Tour ahead of the 4 November local government elections.

During the visit, Hill-Lewis said the focus in local government should always be on ensuring that basic services are working in the municipality.

World.title: 'I was 10' - Scottish survivor speaks out about 86-years-old pedophile teacher
World.content:
LONDON - He was just 10 years old when he was abused by a paedophile teacher, Iain Wares, at a school in Scotland in the 1970s.

Decades later, Neil Douglas is still fighting for justice and helping other survivors do the same.

He has worked with South African advocacy group Women and Men Against Child Abuse to hold 87-year-old Wares to account.

Wares faces justice on two fronts. He was found guilty of sexually and physically abusing a former pupil in South Africa while dozens more charges await him in the United Kingdom.

READ |Convicted paedophile Iain Wares back in court

In an exclusive interview with eNCA, Douglas detailed the abuse he endured when he was in Primary School.

At the time, Wares was his class master and taught two or three subjects a day as well as sports.

“The abuse was daily and went through the entire year,"Douglas recalled".

It was worse when he realised that he was not Wares' only victim.

Some of these instances happened in class, when he called them up to mark their homework.

“His hand would start exploring…”

He said Wares' violence was evident, but nobody in the class could react.

“It was kind of an unwritten rule: We never watched, we never looked. It was heads down.[It could have been that] it was out of respect for the person who was being abused or [one would be] praying please don’t pick me next,”

At that age, he said he did not understand what was happening to him and that Wares masked his behaviour as though he was a ‘dad looking after you’

But somewhere along his experience, Douglas found the courage to speak out.

He said in 2022, the story made it to a radio segment, a moment he said it brought him to tears.

“I just happened to be sitting with a sandwich and heard on the news, and that was the start of the snowball. I contacted the school; they encouraged me to go to the police. I ended up chatting with [broadcaster], discovering other survivors, and ultimately ending up in South Africa to see what's in connection with the local case there against him.”

It was during these times he said he learned about the stigma around South African men who were sexually abused but chose to remain silent because they feared being viewed as ‘damaged goods’

“I thought that my voice if it helps anyone else come forward and say I've been abused, then that's wonderful because they can then get the help that they need.”

Douglas said the abuse he witnessed not only weighed heavily on him as a child, where his academics were impacted, he withdrew from people, was an easy pick for bullies, but as he grew older as well.

“I recognise that I'm hyper-vigilant in some situations. I'm very wary about where I sit and who will sit beside me, who can touch me. I've changed careers a few times. I'm always trying to prove myself to be worth something. I've had a long time with complex PTSD, although that seems to have gone into abeyance at the moment.”

READ | Pre-sentencing for convicted paedophile Iain Wares
