World.title: FlixBus Expands Network to 258 Destinations in Croatia
World.content:
September the 20th, 2026 – The popular coach service FlixBus has expanded its already enviable network to 258 destinations in Croatia.

Croatia is an important part of the Flix Europe East region, and Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe are among the areas with great potential for further development, says Michal Leman from Flix. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that a decade of FlixBus operations in Croatia has now officially been marked. The company began providing services back in 2016 in four Croatian cities and in cooperation with four bus partners, and today in the wider Flix network it has more than 258 connected destinations in Croatia and 390 cities across Europe.

Michal Leman, Vice President Europe East of Flix, emphasises that the anniversary is not only a look back. “Croatia is now entering a new chapter in which we want to further develop domestic and international connectivity, in cooperation with our local partners. Croatia is an important part of the Flix Europe East region, and Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe are among the areas with great potential for further development.

We therefore see the future not only in new lines, but in even stronger partnerships, better connected markets and a greater number of opportunities for passengers,” Leman says. In the first ten years of operations, FlixBus in Croatia has transported 16.3 million passengers, and the growth of the network is best shown by the connectivity data: the number of direct connections to and from Croatia increased from 375 in 2016 to 4,471 in 2026.

The number of bus partners simultaneously rose from four to 15, while during 2026 FlixBus records an average of around 9,100 departures per month. Today a total of 128 lines operate from and to Croatia. Ten years of development has not meant only an increase in the number of lines and destinations, but above all growth in opportunities for passengers – from a greater choice of destinations and travel times to stronger linking of Croatian cities with neighbouring countries and the rest of Europe.

From the very beginning Croatia, was part of a wider story of regional connectivity. Only a year after entering the Croatian market, in 2017, FlixBus expanded to Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia and Slovenia, thereby laying the foundations for stronger connectivity of Central and Southeastern Europe. Flix sees particular potential in Southeastern Europe, where stronger domestic and international connectivity can further bring individual markets closer together, but also better connect them with the rest of the European network.

World.title: The Croatian Bell Tower That Offers Views into Three Countries
World.content:
September the 20th, 2026 – There’s a Croatian bell tower hidden away in an old Istrian town which, on clear days, offers spectacular views into three different countries.

A trip to the gorgeous old settlement of Buje is a perfect combination of history, untouched nature and excellent gastronomy, and nearby are the Momjan castle and the unusual Istrian desert of Piski. Putni kofer/Ivana Vasarevic writes that for all their abundant beauty, very few parts of Croatia look as fairy-tale-like as the interior of Istria. Astonishingly beautiful towns surrounded by untouched nature never cease to delight us, and one of them is certainly Buje. Situated on a fertile hill, in the firm embrace of centuries-old vineyards and olive groves, this Istrian gem was already inhabited in the Bronze Age and today has around 3,000 inhabitants. It is only 13 kilometres from the crystal-clear Adriatic Sea (Umag), and the Slovenian border is also very close.

the guardian of buje

Picchio4ever, Daniele Kovacic – Opera propria

Its ancient population once lived in a fortified hillfort, of which there are as many as about 20 remains in Buje and the surrounding area! A labyrinth of paved streets full of charm will take you to the core of the old town and Freedom Square, where the magnificent Church of St. Servulus and the 15th-century bell tower will greet you. From it, in fine weather, there is a fantastic view of as many as three neighbouring countries: Slovenia, Italy and Austria. This beautiful bell tower is one of the tallest in Istria, and given that it stands at 222 metres above sea level, it was once a lookout and watchtower, so it received the nicknames guardian of the town and watch of Istria. In addition, its image also adorned the town seal from the 13th century.

IT wAS FIRST MENTIONED IN DOCUMENTS AS EARLY AS 981 AS CASTRUM BUGLE

And there is also the bell tower that proudly stands next to the Church of Our Lady of Mercy (St. Mary of Mercy). It dates from the 17th century, is 22 metres high, is adorned with a clock, and at its base there is a characteristic passageway, opposite which is the ethnographic museum. At the same time, in the aforementioned church you can see the sculpture of Our Lady of Mercy, one of the most beautiful wooden statues in Istria. In the Iron Age, the wider area around Buje was inhabited by the Histri, the first documented people to settle on the Istrian peninsula, and the Romans also had their colonies in Terra Magica. In the Middle Ages a fortified medieval town developed, and it is first mentioned in documents, i.e. in a charter of the German-Roman Emperor Otto II, as early as 981 as Castrum Bugle.

THE MAGNIFICENT TOWER wAS ONCE PART OF THE VENETIAN WALLS

At the beginning of the 15th century the entire Buje area came under the rule of the Venetian Republic, and over the next four centuries the magnificent bell tower, the impressive Church of St. Servulus (the town’s patron saint) and the town loggia, which was located on Freedom Square, were built there. To this day, the Tower of St. Martin, which was part of the Venetian walls, has been preserved from that period. And after the fall of the once mighty Venetian empire in 1797, the French, the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy and the Kingdom of Italy successively ruled in Buje. After the end of the Second World War, the town and its surroundings ended up in the Free Territory of Trieste. Its status was settled only in 1954, when it was agreed that the northern part of the Territory, Trieste and the surroundings, would belong to Italy, and the southern part, including Buje, to the then Yugoslavia.

THE ETHNOGRAPHIC MUSEUM iS HOME TO AN OLIVE PROCESSING PLANT AND AN OLD BLACKSMITH’S WORKSHOP

If you find yourself in Buje, also take a look at the aforementioned ethnographic collection in the local museum, which preserves handicrafts of folk material culture from the entire Buje area. It is located in a magnificent four-storey building, and tools, furniture and everything that made up a typical old household, once oriented towards agriculture and ancient crafts, are exhibited in it. Down in the basement, you will find a blacksmith’s workshop and an old olive processing plant, i.e. a press, millstone and stone vessels with wooden lids in which olive oil was stored. Traditional Istrian cuisine and valuable pottery items are exhibited on the first floor, and the greatest attraction of this part of the museum is the hearth, the lifeblood of every Istrian household.

NEARBY LIE THE MEDIEVAL MOMJAN CASTLE AND THE ISTRIAN DESERT OF PISKI

The second and third floors are reserved for a loom and antique carved chests in which clothes and other personal items were kept. In addition to all of the above, the third floor is often used for occasional exhibitions of an ethnographic and historical character. Near Buje are also the picturesque settlement of Momjan with its imposing medieval castle above the Dragonja River and the Istrian desert of Piski, a unique natural phenomenon, i.e. marl dunes, one of the greatest attractions of northwestern Istria that really looks impressive.

tHE HOME OF BEER MISU!

Momjan – Fraxinus Croat

And after sightseeing this magical little town, it is time to explore the wine and olive oil roads of the Buje area. Enjoy the delicious Istrian cuisine and excellent wines, but also the excellent local beer that has been produced since 2013 at the San Servolo brewery in Buje. Only four ingredients are responsible for its perfect taste: barley malt, hops, yeast and natural water from the St. John spring, which is located in the valley of the Mirna River. In the pub you can also taste dishes such as beer soup or beer misu.

World.title: Rusafa Integrity Court recovers 51 billion dinars for Rafidain Bank
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Rusafa Investigation Court Specialized in Integrity and Money Laundering Cases announced on Monday, September 21, 2026, the recovery of 51 billion Iraqi dinars on behalf of state-owned Rafidain Bank.

According to an official statement released by the Supreme Judicial Council’s media office and, the restitution was executed following intensive investigative proceedings into major financial and administrative corruption offenses that directly harmed public finances.

The judiciary noted that the successful clawback forms part of an ongoing, systemic anti-corruption drive designed to safeguard state assets, close institutional vulnerabilities, and enforce accountability across the public banking sector.

Rigorous judicial reviews and forensic audit procedures spearheaded by the specialized court enabled authorities to trace the illicitly acquired funds and return the entire 51 billion dinars to state accounts.

Judicial authorities affirmed that legal actions against the implicated perpetrators remain active, emphasizing that prosecutorial teams will continue pursuing individuals and entities employing unlawful mechanisms to generate illicit profits at the expense of public treasury funds.

World.title: Iraq plans to bring 6 million weapons under state control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An official in the Iraqi Ministry of Interior said on Monday that the government is proceeding with the decision to restrict the possession of weapons exclusively to security forces.

Hussein al-Awadi, the Undersecretary of the Ministry of Interior, confirmed in a statement that the authorities intend to collect up to six million weapons in the coming months, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Bringing arms under state control is a decision firmly adopted by the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces and all Iraqi government security agencies, ensuring that weapons remain exclusively in the hands of official security forces, according to al-Awadi.

In late August, the Iraqi military reaffirmed its commitment to implementing the government’s goal of putting all weapons under state control, stating that it is an irreversible sovereign matter.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is spearheading the government’s proposal to bring all weaponry under strict state control to strengthen national sovereignty, enforce the rule of law, and keep the country out of regional wars.

The effort aims to abolish autonomous armed power by September 30, 2026, when the military mission of the US-led international coalition comes to an end.

Armed factions such as Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Kataib al-Imam Ali have started to sever their autonomous ties to fully integrate into official governmental institutions.

The Iraqi Interior Ministry extended the national weapons registration procedure to the end of 2026 while continuing to purchase medium-range firearms from individuals.

Security personnel are actively targeting unauthorized organizations, carrying out raids and seizing illegal weapons.

Factions such as Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada refuse to disarm as long as any foreign military presence remains in the country.

While foreign forces depart on September 30, security authorities underline that the date symbolizes the beginning of a progressive, long-term weapon control process, rather than an explicit timetable for final disarmament.

World.title: Iraq urges US firms to accelerate project implementation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari urged on Saturday US companies operating in the oil and energy sectors to accelerate the implementation of their projects in the country.

Sari remarks took place during his meeting in Baghdad with US Charge d’Affaires to Iraq Steven Fagin to review bilateral relations and discuss approaches to enhance economic and financial cooperation.

The Iraqi minister’s call aims to boost foreign investment and support the development of vital sectors.

Sari said in a statement that Iraq’s relations with other countries are driven by the country’s supreme interests. He emphasized the Iraqi government’s commitment to maintaining a balanced relationship with the United States based on shared interests.

Fagin described the Iraqi government delegation’s visit to Washington last July as highly successful. He emphasized the importance of building upon the visit’s outcomes to strengthen cooperation between the United States and Iraq.

On July 13, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi paid a five-day visit to the United States, where he signed 48 agreements and memoranda of understanding, as well as announced cooperation between Iraqi and US organizations.

The agreements totaled over $60 billion and encompassed industries such as oil, energy, industry, technology, telecommunications, finance, agriculture, education, and health.

World.title: Spain coach De la Fuente gets new deal after World Cup success
World.content:
Madrid – Spain’s World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente is to sign a new contract keeping him in the role until 2032, the Spanish football federation (RFEF) announced on Monday.

“Luis de la Fuente will extend his contract through the next two European Championships, in 2028 and 2032, as well as the 2030 World Cup,” the RFEF said in a statement.

The 65-year-old, who took charge of Spain in 2022 after replacing Luis Enrique, has since led the national team to World Cup success, Euro 2024 glory and the 2023 UEFA Nations League title.

De la Fuente spent a decade working with Spain’s youth teams before stepping up to the senior role.

“We’re talking about the most successful head coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, this is something Luis de la Fuente deserves, a long-term future at the RFEF,” said Rafael Louzan, chair of the Spanish FA’s board of directors.

Spain travel to England on September 26 in their first game since lifting the World Cup in July before hosting Croatia three days later in Seville, to start their Nations League campaign.

They return home to play the Czech Republic in Oviedo on October 3 and end the international window by heading to Croatia three days later.

World.title: EU proposes energy rating for data centres
World.content:
Brussels – Data centres in Europe will be rated on energy and water consumption under an EU proposal put forward Monday to pre-empt possible public discontent as the bloc pushes to boost its computing capacity.

The European Union is aiming to triple its data centre capacity over the next seven years as it plays catch up with the United States and China on artificial intelligence.

“Tripling our data centre capacity cannot mean tripling the pressure on our grids, our water and our energy bills,” said European Commission vice president for clean transition Teresa Ribera.

Data centre construction has sparked backlash across the United States, with local residents often complaining about the power-hungry engines of AI driving up electricity costs — a hot political issue ahead of November’s midterm elections.

The EU said its scheme would provide the public with information about the water and energy consumption of sites with capacity above 500 kW, which already have to report key performance metrics to the EU.

Similarly to that already in use for home appliances, the rating will rank data centres on a coloured scale where A/Green is the most efficient and G/red the least efficient, according to a commission presentation.

To encourage good practices, the score will take into account data centres’ contribution to the grid, such as the reuse of waste heat and the addition of clean energy generation capacities, the commission said.

“Efficient, flexible, powered by additional clean energy and reusing waste heat, this is how data centres become an asset for (the) EU’s energy transition,” Ribera added.

Data centres are yet to become a flashpoint political issue in the 27-nation EU, as the bloc lags well behind the United States on AI development.

The slower growth is in part due to already-high-energy costs, which weigh on European businesses and families alike.

But the International Energy Agency estimates the fast expanding sector will account for more than three percent of overall electricity demand in the EU by 2030.

“To ensure that the digital transformation truly works for our society, we must address the growing energy demand of data centres,” said the EU’s energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen.

“Understanding their energy and resource consumption is the essential first step towards integrating them sustainably into our energy system.”

The labels will be automatically generated by the EU based on companies’ reporting and will be accessible on an EU database, with the first expected to appear in 2027, Brussels said.

The commission said it was also looking into setting minimum performance standards for data centres.

World.title: Putin’s party secures record score in Russia election
World.content:
Moscow – Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party won a record supermajority in the Duma, authorities announced Monday after a tightly controlled three-day election without parties critical of the Kremlin or the war in Ukraine.

Electoral chief Ella Pamfilova said preliminary results showed United Russia — which has dominated Russian politics for 25 years — won 355 of the Duma’s 450 seats.

The result handed Putin’s party an increased supermajority and beat its previous record of 343 seats. The supermajority means it can change the constitution, if it needs to.

The Kremlin said the result of the first parliamentary election since Moscow sent troops to Ukraine in 2022 showed Russians were united around Putin, who has been in power since New Year’s Eve 1999.

The conflict has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and hit ordinary lives in Russia more than ever this year. Moscow has banned criticism of its military campaign and the only party that called for an end to the war was removed from the election.

“These indicators, of course, point to the highest level of consolidation within Russian society around the head of state,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a briefing with journalists.

Elections under Putin are tightly controlled and few in Russia doubted United Russia would win.

Putin had encouraged Russians to vote in support of troops in Ukraine and Moscow also organised voting in occupied Ukraine.

Pamfilova said turnout was over 59 percent, thanking Russians for voting despite what she called “psychological pressure on Russia.”

Russia’s Ukraine campaign broke its ties with the West. Kyiv hit Moscow with its biggest drone attack of the war Sunday, the last day of voting, killing two people and setting an oil refinery ablaze.

“Despite the extreme situation, we were successful in ensuring the maximum security of these elections,” Pamfilova told a Moscow press conference, thanking security services for ensuring the vote went ahead.

– Fifth year of war –

The election result is expected to further tighten Putin’s grip on power.

Some fear a new military mobilisation in Russia. Putin has denied this is in the works, while Kyiv accuses Moscow of planning a callup in coming weeks.

Russia’s Communist party came second in the vote, winning 40 seats. The nationalist LDPR party took 25 seats and the New People party won 20.

The election took place amid the escalation of the Ukraine war in recent months, with no diplomatic solution in sight.

For the Kremlin, it served as a barometer on the mood of Russians towards the war.

In some regions, voting also took place for the heads of regions.

In Chechnya, Ramzan Kadyrov — known for ruling the Muslim-majority republic with an iron fist — won 99.85 percent of the vote, the electoral commission said.

Opposing Kadyrov is hugely dangerous in Chechnya, which is known for extra-judicial killings.

Putin’s political opponents are in exile, prison or dead — such as his main opponents Alexei Navalny who died in an Arctic prison in 2024.

The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas dismissed Russia’s “so-called” election.

“The Kremlin silenced dissent, barred the only registered party that opposed its war in Ukraine, and shut out international election monitors. The veneer of democracy is all that remains in Russia,” Kallas said.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 35% of shipments leaving Hormuz last week
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Data from Kpler, a leading data platform that tracks commodity flows and maritime shipping, indicates a decline in shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz over the past week, with the number of vessels traversing this vital waterway remaining low.

13 oil tankers departed the Strait of Hormuz during the week that started on September 13, carrying a total of approximately 34 million barrels of crude oil.

Saudi Arabia accounted for approximately half of the exports, while Iraq contributed 35 percent of the total crude oil shipments that left the Strait of Hormuz that week.

Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly lower than pre-war levels; prior to the outbreak of the war on February 28, the vital waterway typically handled around 125 large commercial vessels daily.oil,

Over the weekend, 12 commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz, compared to 35 the previous weekend, amid ongoing tensions in the Gulf region and a disagreement between the United States and Iran.

Visible shipping traffic through the strait, which previously served as a conduit for one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, has decreased significantly. However, Middle Eastern producers continue to export oil on tankers with their transponders switched off.

World.title: Spanish PM says unregulated AI could be ‘devastating’
World.content:
Madrid – Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday joined a chorus of calls to regulate AI as safety fears around the technology escalate, warning of potentially “devastating” consequences.

The debate over the risks from artificial intelligence has intensified this month, with many of the industry’s leading lights voicing support for more cooperation, regulation and slower development of the technology.

Former employees of major AI companies have resigned warning of the technology’s risks, even pointing to an existential threat to humanity.

“If artificial intelligence is concentrated among a few companies and a handful of countries, its impact on shared prosperity, and therefore on the idea of democracy, will be very negative, if not devastating,” Sanchez told an AI-focused event in Madrid.

“We must act urgently, because unregulated, opaque artificial intelligence running wild… and in very few hands is the perfect recipe for disaster,” added the Socialist leader.

US President Donald Trump — with whom Sanchez has repeatedly clashed — has dismissed fears that AI could wipe out humanity and rejected calls to put greater controls around the fast-moving technology.

Sanchez, an outspoken critic of the power of big tech companies and their bosses, on Monday renewed his criticism of “techno-oligarchs” and urged international coordination on AI.

“Self-regulation does not work”, said Sanchez, calling for an AI “focused on well-being and collective prosperity that enables the building of fairer societies”.

He presented a 12-month plan aiming for “a new social contract for artificial intelligence” in Spain in cooperation with civil society.

This agreement would have to offer “security to people in the face of the changes in work and in life that this technology will entail”, he said.

In February, Sanchez announced a plan to ban social media for under-16s, sparking a spat with X owner Elon Musk and Telegram founder Pavel Durov.

His government has also asked the Spanish prosecutors to investigate X, Meta and TikTok for possible offences related to AI-generated child pornography.

World.title: No median cuts, surface intersections on future high-speed NH corridors: NHAI
World.content:
A view of the Barapullah Phase-3 elevated corridor that is scheduled to be inaugurated on September 29, 2026, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)

NEW DELHI: New access-controlled high-speed national highway corridors will have no median (divider) openings and no at-grade (surface level) intersections, a move that aims at eliminating conflict points and reducing crashes.It has also been mandated under new NHAI guidelines issued on Monday that these corridors wonât have raised concrete dividers but flush medians â painted centre lanes with thick wire ropes or crash barriers. These will also have advance exit signage at 5 km, 2 km, 1 km and 500 metres to help motorists prepare for lane changes well in advance.The design provisions are aimed at improving safety on access-controlled corridors where cars are allowed to travel at speeds of up to 100 kmph. Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, Ambala-Kotputli corridor and Trans-Haryana corridor are among such highways.NHAI said the guidelines seek to bring uniformity in the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed corridors and ensure consistency in technical standards across projects.âThe guidelines will apply to all upcoming four-lane and six-lane greenfield and brownfield access-controlled high-speed national highways,â an NHAI spokesperson said.Officials said eliminating median cuts and surface intersections will prevent dangerous cross movements and wrong-side driving, while standardised signage and geometric design will improve traffic flow and reduce the risk of high-speed crashes on the new generation of national highway corridors.The move is significant as govt has set a target of developing 50,000 km of access-controlled high-speed corridors over the coming years.At present, there are no separate standards governing the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed national highways, except for expressways. The new document fills that gap by laying down dedicated norms for highways that are access-controlled but not classified as expressways.The guidelines also specify lane configuration based on detailed traffic assessment and future traffic projections. Depending on the expected traffic volume and the number of structures such as bridges, flyovers and interchanges, these corridors will have a right of way of 60 metres or 70 metres.

World.title: UP Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak hears public grievances at Janta Darshan
World.content:

The complaints raised during the hearing included issues related to medical treatment, financial assistance, police matters, revenue, family disputes and other administrative concerns.

Pathak heard the complaints and contacted the concerned officials over the phone, directing them to take action in accordance with applicable rules and eligibility criteria.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami says strong cooperatives, M-PACS can strengthen rural economy
World.content:
DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday said strengthening cooperatives and M-PACS can play a key role in boosting the rural economy, supporting mountain agriculture and creating opportunities for youth in the state.

Virtually addressing the inaugural session of the Shri Laxmanrao Inamdar Second Cooperative Leadership Training Programme at Pantnagar, Dhami stressed the need for skilled leadership to make cooperatives an effective instrument of economic empowerment.

The programme was organised by Sahakar Bharati Uttarakhand at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar.

Paying tribute to Sahakar Bharati founder Shri Laxmanrao Inamdar on his birth anniversary, CM Dhami said such training programmes would play an important role in strengthening the rural economy by empowering the cooperative sector.

He said, "Strong leadership will strengthen M-PACS, strong M-PACS will strengthen villages, and strong villages will make Uttarakhand prosperous."

The chief minister said several important initiatives aimed at giving a new direction to the cooperative movement had been launched from Pantnagar, the land of knowledge. The launch of the Sahakar Granth, the Devbhoomi Sarathi initiative of the State Cooperative Federation, new courses in the cooperative sector, a social media reels campaign to connect youth with cooperatives, and the M-PACS leadership training programme would give fresh momentum to the cooperative sector, he said.





CM Dhami said the state government is committed to taking Uttarakhand rapidly forward towards the vision of "Samriddhi through Cooperatives".

He said cooperatives can serve as an effective means of addressing several challenges faced by the hill state, including migration, strengthening mountain agriculture, providing markets for local products and boosting the rural economy.

He said primary agricultural cooperative societies (PACS) are an important pillar of the state's cooperative system and are being strengthened as M-PACS to make them more capable and effective in line with changing requirements.

The state government is working to provide better facilities to farmers through M-PACS, create new opportunities for youth and strengthen rural areas economically, he added.

The chief minister said skilled and visionary leadership is essential to make M-PACS more effective, and the leadership training programme has been launched with this objective. Training, he said, is not merely a means of enhancing knowledge but also a powerful tool for developing new perspectives, approaches and direction among leaders.

CM Dhami said connecting farmers, youth and women with the cooperative movement is a priority of the state government. The government is working to make cooperatives not merely limited to societies, but an effective instrument of public participation and economic empowerment, he said.

He called upon the representatives participating in the training programme to further strengthen the spirit of cooperation in their respective areas and encourage more people to join the movement.

He said all stakeholders must work together to make cooperatives a people's movement, strengthen villages, create opportunities for youth and enhance the economic strength of farmers.

World.title: The 'chosen one' for a role in BSP is Ishan: Mayawati's latest U-turn in ongoing family drama
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Mayawatiâs chosen one is Ishan Anand. Or is he? Well, at least for now. Thereâs another twist in the ongoing succession drama in the BSP chiefâs family. Younger nephew Ishan, who was ruled out from getting any position in the BSP only ten days back, has ended up winning Mayawatiâs âtrust testâ for a role in the party.

âOnly Shri Ishan Anand from Shri Anand Kumarâs family will now be promoted by giving him a respectable responsibility in the party,â Mayawati announced on X on Sunday.

So, when the BSP holds its national-level meeting in Lucknow on September 23, Ishan is likely to get a ârespectable responsibilityâ in the party. This will be 20 days after his elder brother Akash Anand was shown the door at a similar meeting held on September 3.

Ishan, Akash and their sister Deepika are children of Mayawatiâs younger brother Anand Kumar, who has been âworking in Mayawatiâs service for many years.â

A warning for Ishan

But Ishanâs promotion comes with a strict rider. He has to ârise above attachment to his brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication.â

There was a clear and strong warning for Ishan. âIf he commits any serious act against the party, he too will be shown the door from the party.





But in such a situation, no other member of Shri Anand Kumarâs family will be given any responsibility, big or small, in the party,â Mayawati announced.

Niece loses the race

In a long post on X on September 12, the BSP chief had ruled out any political role for her nephews Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, but left room for Deepika to take on responsibilities in the party if the need arises.

The BSP chief had said, "Today it is my final decision and pledge that in return, none of his sons, in particular, will be allowed to engage in politics by holding any position, big or small, within the BSP.

If Anand Kumar, while remaining with me, needs another member to assist him, then in the current political situation, he can seek the help of his only daughter, Kumari Deepika Anand, who is currently studying law. He can then, based on her honesty, loyalty, and efficiency, assign her his own responsibilities within the party as needed.

"

But that did not happen.

In her post, Mayawati dwelled on the âdilemmaâ she faced in making the decision and also shared the yardstick she used to decide the âchosen one.â

âThe question of who from Shri Anand Kumarâs family I should or should not promote in the party has been a matter of considerable dilemma for me for some time. Bringing this dilemma to an end, and after giving serious thought to every aspect, I have now decided that if any member of his family is to be promoted in the party, it should be someone who does not follow Akashâs footsteps in any way.â

âAs for seeking help from his daughter in the future, after she gets married, if her case also turns out to be like Shri Akash Anandâs, that too would not be in the interest of the party.

Keeping such a possibility in mind, it would now be appropriate in the interest of the party to completely keep Shri Akash Anand and his sister away from being given any responsibility in the party. In other words, there will be no change whatsoever in this decision,â Mayawati wrote in her post.

Doors forever closed for Akash Anand?

Akash Anand, who was groomed for years and, at least on two occasions in the past, announced as Mayawatiâs âpolitical successor,â now seems completely out of the picture.

At least for now.

âOn special request of Shri Anand Kumar, I had to promote his elder son, Shri Akash Anand, in politics. Since his marriage, however, Shri Akash Anandâs conduct and activities at every step have been such that, a few days ago, I once again had to separate him from the party,â Mayawati said in her latest post.

âIn other words, he is now completely caught up in the web of his father-in-law, Shri Ashok Siddharth.

Bringing him back into the party now would amount to a major betrayal of the party, and I can never commit such an act against the party,â she wrote.

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.

In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra.

The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.

Mayawati appointed him BSPâs national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.

However, now with his younger brother taking the centre stage, it may not be easy for Akash to claw back into the power structure.

The Kanshi Ram reference

The BSP chief shared her mantra for success in politics. âI want to tell the people of the party that, keeping my own experience in mind, if they want to succeed in politics and do something for society, they must, like me, rise above their attachment to their brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication,â Mayawati wrote in the post.

She then referred to the role of BSP founder Kanshi Ram in showing her the path

âThe founder and architect of the BSP, respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji, after entering politics, always kept himself away from giving political benefits to his close relatives and family members.

He allowed them to work in the party organisation only with a selfless spirit. Not only this, he devoted his entire life to the interests and welfare of the âBahujan Samajâ, without creating a family of his own,â Maywati wrote.

âInspired by him, I too decided to follow in his footsteps and devoted my entire life to the âBahujan Samajâ. However, because I am a woman, I was compelled to always keep one of my brothers or sisters with me.

Under this arrangement, my younger brother, Shri Anand Kumar, has been working in my service for many years,â the BSP chief said.

The Ambedkar example

Justifying her move, Mayawati wrote, âI have taken this decision in the interest of the party and the movement, inspired by respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji and influenced by a letter written by the revered Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar.â

The BSP chief stated that Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar had written a letter on February 23, 1956, warning his son Yashwant B Ambedkar over his alleged attempts to try and take control of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press.

To convey her message to Ishan and others, Mayawati cited the strong stand taken by Ambedkar against his son, âI have to inform you that I have received several communications from Shri Upsham saying that you are not allowing him to perform his duties as the accountant and cashier of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press. You seem to think that by doing this you will take control of the press. I am warning you that the press is public property; it belongs neither to you nor to me, and it is not possible to permit any kind of irregularity in a public account.

Your conduct has not been proper... If you do not heed my final and last instructions, I will remove you from the press and, if you do not heed this warning, I will also prosecute you.â

Road ahead for Ishan

âUneasy lies the head that wears a crownâ: Well, thatâs perhaps how one can describe Ishanâs future in BSP. We will have to wait and see what respectable role he gets from Mayawati on September 23 when the party meets. However, irrespective of the role, the road ahead for Ishan would be challenging.

World.title: 'BJP's Punjab conspiracy exposed': Sanjay Singh alleges drug trafficker Jagga was called 'Bhai' by BJP, being portrayed as revolutionary
World.content:
"BJPâs Punjab conspiracy exposed": Sanjay Singh alleges drug trafficker Jagga was called âBhaiâ by BJP, being portrayed as revolutionary

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Aam Aadmi Party on Monday alleged a conspiracy by the BJP, ShiromAkali Dal and Congress to defame Punjab and undermine the Bhagwant Mann government's campaign against drugs.Senior party leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh said Jagga Singh, whom the BJP has referred to as its "bhai", has nine cases registered against him, including under the NDPS (Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances) Act, while eight cases are registered against Mohan Jeet Singh.Addressing a press conference at the AAP headquarters on Monday, Singh said that the BJP, Congress and Akali Dal are jointly hatching a deep conspiracy in Punjab."A complete conspiracy is being planned to defame the campaign being run by CM Bhagwant Mann and the AAP government against drugs in Punjab, weaken it, stop it, and ensure that Punjab is defamed across the world for drugs," he added.The AAP MP added, "There are three characters in this conspiracy, Jagga Singh, Mohanjeet Singh and Gulzar Singh. The Congress, BJP and Akali Dal, without knowing the truth or conducting any investigation, are using these people and standing behind them to make bizarre statements and run campaigns against the AAP government."Sanjay Singh said that Jagga Singh, whom the BJP and Congress are presenting as a revolutionary and claiming was running a campaign against drugs and was forced to consume poison as a result, has nine cases registered against him."Jagga Singh has already been convicted in four of these nine cases, and cases of rape, kidnapping and drug trafficking are also registered against him," he added.He continued, "Two gram panchayats had formally passed resolutions against drugs, because his business was unable to operate, as he himself had been involved in the drug trade. The Congress, BJP and Akali Dal are portraying him as a revolutionary and claiming that the government is harassing him."The AAP MP highlighted that the second person is Mohanjeet Singh, who had shown a black flag to Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann. He said the Congress, BJP and Akali Dal are running a campaign claiming that this warrior fighting against drugs was brutally beaten merely for showing a black flag. The reality, he said, is that eight FIRs are registered against Mohanjeet Singh."The third name is Gulzar, about whom it was claimed that he took his own life because of Minister Harpal Singh Cheema. The reality is that opposition parties in Punjab kept making Gulzar record videos and drove him around in a car until he made a statement against the AAP. In the first video Gulzar recorded, he did not mention Harpal Singh Cheema or the AAP. However, in a subsequent video, he named Harpal Singh Cheema. This shows that opposition parties pressured and used him, which led to his present condition," Singh said.He said, "I want to tell the Congress, BJP and Akali Dal not to indulge in such filthy politics and not to try to defame Punjab by making baseless and false allegations. The AAP government is running its campaign against drugs with complete commitment and is eliminating drugs."Sanjay Singh said that he was also aware of the period when drug mafias had links with leaders of the Akali Dal and BJP. He said the Akali Dal, BJP and Congress had together conducted the drug trade in Punjab and committed the sin of delivering drugs to every village."Sanjay Singh claimed that under the rule of these parties, the drug trade continued to flourish and governments provided protection to drug dealers."Punjab has also witnessed a period when, under the Akali Dal-BJP government, young children studying in high school and intermediate classes died because of drugs," he added."Drugs worth Rs 20,000 crore were seized at Adani's Mundra Port in BJP-ruled Gujarat. This was stated by the central government agency NIA. The NIA had approached the Supreme Court to oppose the bail of those arrested in connection with the drug trade. While opposing their bail, the NIA stated in an affidavit that the money from the drugs worth Rs 20,000 crore seized at Adani's port in Gujarat was spent on training terrorists in Pakistan," Singh said."The NIA has submitted a written affidavit before the Supreme Court opposing bail for the accused, stating that they should not be granted bail because they were very serious criminals and the money from the drugs was being used to train terrorists in Pakistan," the MP added.He noted, "Gujarat has a liquor ban and alcohol is completely prohibited there, yet 100 people died after consuming poisonous liquor, while PM Narendra Modi and Nitin Nabin did not utter a single word. In neighbouring Uttar Pradesh, 105 people died after consuming poisonous liquor in Aligarh, but not a single BJP leader said a word."Therefore, he said, BJP leaders should not try to defame Punjab, because the entire country knows them and they will be exposed across the country.Singh concluded by highlighting that the Akali Dal, BJP and Congress have themselves run the largest drug trade in Punjab. If any party has genuinely taken action against it, he said, it is the AAP and the Bhagwant Mann government."If these parties want to speak openly about this issue, we will do so, but we will not allow them to defame Punjab. Those who themselves are disgraced and against whom cases of rape, kidnapping and drug trafficking are registered are being used by these parties for politics, with the parties standing behind them," he said.

World.title: ‘PM Modi assured me’: OP Rajbhar’s claim on UP division revives decades-old debate
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that Prime Minister

assured him that the state would be divided into four parts, reviving a nearly two-decade-old debate over dividing the country's most populous state.

Rajbhar, who heads

ally Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), claimed that PM Modi told him Uttar Pradesh could be divided after the caste census.

âWe want to assure you regarding the 27% reservation. I spoke with the prime minister about this,â he told the audience at an SBSP programme in Deoria on Sunday.

âHe (PM Modi) said, âOm Prakash ji, your point is justified, but some people are opposing it.â I asked him how we could move forward, and he replied, âI will conduct a caste census, and once we have counted the castes, there will be no difficulty.â

The state will be divided into four parts. And on the day the Purvanchal is formed, if the chief minister is to be from any caste, then a Rajbharâs son will become the chief minister,â he added.

However, another UP minister and BJP ally, Sanjay Nishad, dismissed Rajbharâs remarks as âmisleadingâ, saying the Nishad Party was not in favour of a reorganisation.

âThere had been a demand to divide UP earlier, but now the state is progressing rapidly in all spheres.





Further, special development funds have been allocated for regions like Bundelkhand and Purvanchal that needed handholding,â Nishad told PTI.

Rajbhar has advocated the division of Uttar Pradesh in the past as well,

that the âstate can be developed only after it is divided into four parts.â

When Mayawati proposed carving out four states from UP

With the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due in early 2027, Rajbharâs remarks have revived the long-running political debate over dividing the state.

Ahead of the 2012 UP assembly elections, then chief minister Mayawati revived the demand, with the state assembly passing a resolution to split Uttar Pradesh into Avadh Pradesh, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand and Paschim Pradesh.

In 2011, her government had sent a proposal to the Congress-led Centre seeking the creation of the four states.

Before that, in 2008, Mayawati had proposed dividing Uttar Pradesh into three parts.

Several parties, including the Rashtriya Lok Dal and Congress, have also backed demands for dividing the state at various points. There have additionally been calls for a separate Bundelkhand comprising parts of Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring Madhya Pradesh.

Uttar Pradesh was last divided in 2000, when the BJP-led central government carved out Uttarakhand, then known as Uttaranchal.

Why Uttar Pradesh matters

With a population of around 25 crore, Uttar Pradesh is Indiaâs most populous state.

If it were an independent country, its population would make it the fifth- or sixth-most populous country in the world.

Geographically, Uttar Pradesh is the fourth-largest state in India.

It sends 80 members to the 543-seat Lok Sabha, the highest representation of any state or Union territory. Its legislative assembly has 403 members.

Six prime ministers were born in Uttar Pradesh, while several others, including Narendra Modi, have represented the state in Parliament.

World.title: The 'rebel' hit by rebellion: How Mamata Banerjee's TMC journey has come full circle
World.content:
's political journey in West Bengal has come almost full circle.

In 1998, Mamata walked out of the Congress after years of differences with its leadership and formed the

. She believed the Congress was not doing enough to challenge the Left Front, which had been ruling West Bengal for decades.

28 years later, Didi, as she is fondly called, is now herself a step away from losing control of her party to a rebellion. Her

Congress has split, and rivals in the party, who once worked under her are now challenging her control. The Election Commission has temporarily frozen the party's original name and its well-known 'Jora Ghash Phul' (flowers and grass) symbol while it decides which faction has the ârealâ claim.

And what's more! In an interesting turn of events, Mamata is now desperately banking on the Congressâs support to survive the BJPâs political offensive against her in West Bengal.

The change comes at a difficult moment for her.

The BJP recently ended Trinamoolâs 15-year rule in West Bengal in May, crossing 200 seats and forming its first government in the state. Mamataâs party, which had been in power for 15 years, fell below 100 seats.

Mamata's troubles have only grown since then.

The defeat was followed by a rebellion within the

TMC

and finally a battle over who has the right to use the partyâs name and symbol.





For a leader who built her career as a rebel, Mamata is now facing a rebellion of her own.

Mamata on TMC symbol row

Congress: From bitter rival to 'sister party'

At the peak of her power-packed 15 years as chief minister of West Bengal, Mamata refused to acknowledge the presence of Congress in West Bengal. In fact, for Mamata, both the Congress and the Left were bitter political rivals and she would often accuse them of being the B-team of the BJP in the state. But that changed in the aftermath of her crushing defeat in May this year as the BJP swept the stateâs political landscape and formed its first government.

The shift in power dynamics was on display when Mamata announced support for the Congress candidate in the Nandigram bypoll to be held on October 6. "We are extending our support to Congress in Nandigram. We are doing this for the greater interest of the nation,â Mamata Banerjee announced. But what really surprised was her reference to the Congress as a ânatural allianceâ and a âsister partyâ. Words that would sound almost alien to those who have followed Mamataâs politics, especially the Congress leaders in the state.

While the Congress has strongly backed her fight against the Election Commission, with Rahul Gandhi leading the charge, the help is unlikely to transform into a greater alliance, at least for now. The West Bengal Congress unit, which was at the receiving end of Mamataâs political aggression for many years, is very clear and categorical that it does not want any alliance with her party.

Rahul Gandhi backs Mamata Banerjee

Vendetta politics

Since losing power, Mamata has repeatedly accused the BJP of targeting her and trying to weaken her party.

The irony is that Mamata herself faced similar accusations after she came to power in 2011, ending 34 years of Left rule. Both the Left and the Congress had accused the Trinamool of using political pressure and defections to weaken its rivals.

The circumstances may be different, but the roles have now reversed. What is happening today to her is what she did to her opponents in the past in West Bengal.

Mamata's beginning in politics

Mamata started her political career with the Congress in the 1970s.

The first glimpse of her aggressive political style was on display during Emergency days when she made headlines for her protest against Jay Prakash Narayan.

She quickly rose through the Congress ranks and, in 1984, emerged as the giant killer when she defeated veteran Communist politician Somnath Chatterjee, to win the Jadavpur parliamentary Constituency in West Bengal. She was also among the youngest MPs elected that year.

There has been no looking back since then. She lost in 1989, but came back strongly in 1991 from the Calcutta South constituency and retained the seat in 1996, 1998, 1999, 2004 and 2009 Lok Sabha elections.

From Congress activist and street fighter to TMC founder and three-term West Bengal chief minister

The protest politics and the birth of Trinamool Congress

Mamata's differences with the Congress grew through the 1990s. She believed the party was not aggressive enough in taking on the Left government in West Bengal.

Her politics was built around street protests and agitations against the Left government.

One of the most prominent moments of her political career came in 1993, as state Youth Congress chief, when she led a march to Writersâ Building demanding voter ID cards to prevent alleged electoral malpractice.

Police opened fire during the protest, killing 13 Congress workers. By 1997, her differences with the Congress leadership had reached a breaking point. In 1998, Mamata walked out and formed the Trinamool Congress.

Years later, the Singur and Nandigram movements turned that protest politics into a force strong enough to bring her to power for a good 15 years.

Nandigram challenge, once again

Nandigram has always had a special place in Mamata's political career. The land protests here in 2007 helped turn her into the strongest challenger to the Left. Four years later, she came to power.

But Nandigram also became one of her biggest electoral setbacks. In the 2021 assembly election, Mamata chose to contest from the seat against her former aide Suvendu Adhikari, who had joined the BJP.

Nandigram was Suvenduâs bastion and Mamata wanted to prove a point. That did not happen as she lost to Suvendu by around 2,000 votes. But her Trinamool Congress returned to power in the state with a thumping majority.

Five years later, in 2026, it was Suvenduâs turn to challenge Mamata in her bastion of Bhabanipur, while also contesting from Nandigram. Suvendu not just reinforced his dominance in Nandigram but also humiliated Mamata in Bhabanipur.

Suvendu retained Bhabanipur and vacated Nandigram, necessitating a bypoll. But this time around Mamata faced a setback even before the contest could begin. Her candidate for the October 6 bypoll in Nandigram withdrew from the contest after meeting chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, leaving Mamata without a candidate of her own. She then announced support for Congress candidate Milan Pradhan.

For Mamata, Nandigram has now seen almost every phase of her politics.

It helped her rise, handed her a personal defeat, and is now showing the challenges she faces after losing power.

The road ahead ...

For Mamata, the road ahead is not just about fighting the BJP. The former chief minister has a larger issue at hand at the moment. She has to hold her party together, fight for control of the Trinamool name and symbol, and rebuild her position as the main opposition force in Bengal.

Congress support could help her on some issues, especially at the national level, but a wider alliance in Bengal seems unlikely, at least for now.

Congress leaders in West Bengal remain wary of Mamata after years of on-and-off rivalry and large-scale defections from their party to the Trinamool under Mamataâs watch.

That leaves Mamata at the junction of perhaps the most difficult phase of her political career.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

She began as a Congress leader, broke away in rebellion, built a party of her own and eventually ruled Bengal for 15 years. Now, with rebels challenging that very party and she being forced to return to Congress for help, Mamata's journey has indeed come almost full circle.

The future and fate of the original Trinamool Congress is now in the hands of the Election Commission. Mamata will be keeping her fingers crossed. And rightly so. Precedents from recent past in Maharashtra would worry her. Sharad Pawar lost control of the Nationalist Congress Party and Uddhav Thackeray of Shiv Sena, after the ECI ruled in favour of rebels who had split the two parties. So, will Mamata be lucky, or will she now be left with a âfootball playerâ to try another round of âkhelaâ in West Bengal? Can Mamata once again fight adversity for a much-needed comeback? Well, we will have to wait and watch.

World.title: U.S. halts flights at busy East Coast airports, says fiber line cut at construction site
World.content:
The Federal Aviation Administration ​halted flights at busy East Coast airports in New York, ‌Philadelphia and Boston on Monday (September 21, 2026), saying ​a fiber cable was accidentally cut at ⁠a construction site in New Jersey, U.S.A.

Ground stops were issued for John F. Kennedy Airport and LaGuardia airports, as ‌well as an airport in Teterboro, New Jersey, as 130 world leaders and dozens ‌of ministers are arriving in New York for ‌the ⁠annual high-level meeting of the United Nations ⁠General Assembly.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters a backup fiber line had been cut accidentally by a construction crew ​in New Jersey, prompting significant ‌flight cuts.

He said a new circuit would be operational imminently. It was not clear when the ground stops at the New York-area airports would ‌be lifted.

FlightAware, a flight-tracking site, said ​more than 600 flights at Newark and Philadelphia, or more than 20%, had been delayed ⁠at Philadelphia Terminal Radar Approach Control. Newark is a major United Airlines hub, while Philadelphia is ‌an American Airlines hub.

The issue has also forced the diversion of a number of flights to other airports. Flightradar24, a flight-tracking site, said flights were being delayed by an average of 112 minutes at Newark.

In May 2025, the facility that guides ‌air traffic in and out of Newark Airport suffered a ​series of significant communications outages.

The FAA said last year a telecommunications outage impacted communications and ⁠radar displays at Philadelphia TRACON.

Last year, Congress approved $12.5 ⁠billion to address the aging air traffic control system and boost controller hiring following decades ‌of complaints over airport congestion and flight delays and a series of technology issues in ​recent years.

World.title: BDCC bank waiting for govt. sanction for recruitment, says MLA
World.content:
The Belagavi district central cooperative bank is waiting for the State government approval to fill vacancies of officers and staff, Balachandra Jarkiholi, MLA, said in Belagavi on Monday.

He hoped that the government would approve of the bank’s recruitment proposals in the next few months and the recruitment drive would be completed before December. He was speaking at the 105th annual general body meeting of the bank.

“We had begun the process for filling 134 vacant posts earlier, but the government cancelled it due to certain irregularities in the reservation roaster and other technicalities. Over 21,000 candidates had applied for these posts. We will rectify any error regarding reservation norms from the previous process and seek fresh applications,” he said.

The bank has now sent a new proposal to recruit 134 staff members, comprising 110 clerks, 23 peons, and one security guard. Applications will be invited again once the government approval is received.

“Decisions regarding the sanctioning of loans to sugar factories must be taken after carefully examining all pros and cons. There are approximately 50 sugar factories across the Belagavi, Vijayapura, and Bagalkot districts. The interests of sugarcane growers can be safeguarded only if these factories remain operational. The closure of even a single factory would create difficulties for farmers,” he said.

Annasaheb Jolle, bank chairman and former MP, stated that the bank, with a history spanning over 106 years, is currently celebrating its centenary. Agricultural loans provided to farmers at zero interest have increased from ₹3,300 crore to ₹3,727 crore. Deposits rose by ₹616 crore in six months, reaching ₹6,703 crore. He added that working capital has increased to ₹9,776 crore, and the loan repayment rate stands at 99.78%. The loan limit for sugarcane cultivation has been raised from ₹40,000 to ₹50,000 per acre, providing farmers in Belagavi district with access to an additional ₹700 crore in credit. Farmers are also being supported through loans for tractors, dairy farming, and pipeline installations. He stated that the coverage of the Yashasvini health insurance scheme has been extended to 2.82 lakh members.

He mentioned that digital banking services are being expanded, with micro-ATM facilities provided at five Primary Agricultural Credit Cooperative Societies. Measures have been taken to control non-performing assets (NPAs), and action under the SARFAESI Act is proceeding in cases of long-standing arrears.

Bank directors and officers were present.

World.title: Belagavi students trained by zilla panchayat get into premier institutions
World.content:

As many as eight students from various government PU colleges in the district achieved excellent ranks in the current year’s JEE and NEET examinations.

Rahul Shinde, ZP CEO, has congratulated the students, their teachers and the ZP staff that conducted training sessions and mock tests under the ‘CET-Saksham’ for the 2024-25 academic year.

Partha Akkole and Srihantha Bangari, students of the Government Pre-University College at Majalatti in Chikkodi Taluk, have been admitted to IIT Dhanbad (Jharkhand) and IIT Rourkela (Odisha), respectively.

Srushti Dasar and Varsha Gadad from the Government PU College in Bailhongal secured admissions to medical colleges in Shivamogga and Kalaburagi.

Four students from the Government Pre-University College in Majalatti, Chikkodi taluk, have secured medical seats: Lakshmi Badiger in the government medical college in Karwar, Priya Maradi to Sridevi Medical College in Tumakuru, Pushpa Obannavar to the government medical college in Chamarajanagar, and Keerthi Karikatti to BMCRI Medical College in Bengaluru.

Since the 2024-25 academic year, the ZP has been organising offline mock CET exams. These 80-mark consolidated exams (20 marks per subject) are conducted via OMR sheets — on the second Saturday of every month for I PU students and on the fourth Saturday for II PU students from government colleges. Results are announced the following Monday, and online doubt-clearing sessions are organized on Tuesdays.

In the 2025-26 academic year, as an upgraded component of the programme, an entrance exam was conducted for science students of the Government Pre-University Science College, Majalatti, and the Government Pre-University Science College, Bailahongala. Based on the results, the best students were selected for the Super-50 programme.

Under the ‘Super-500’ programme, a select group of 100 students received specialised capacity-building training to effectively prepare for the NEET and JEE examinations. As part of this training, students regularly took offline mock tests using OMR sheets, simulating the actual exam format.

In addition to the mock test training, a campus visit to IIT Dharwad was organised on November 18, 2025. During the visit, students attended a guidance session and participated in practical training sessions.

World.title: New DUSU office-bearers visit Satya Niketan, promise action on housing issues
World.content:
The three newly elected Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) office-bearers from the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) visited Satya Niketan on Monday to pay tribute to the students who lost their lives in the September 6 building collapse and promised to address students’ accommodation issues.

In a statement, the ABVP said, “Upon arriving there, the office-bearers pledged that the new students’ union would continuously struggle to resolve the issues faced by students living in Satya Niketan and surrounding areas and protect their rights. They also vowed to make every positive effort to ensure such incidents do not recur in the future.”

New DUSU president Yash Dabas said the practice of charging arbitrary rents and depriving students of basic amenities in Satya Niketan was a serious issue.

ABVP Delhi State secretary Sarthak Sharma said the election victory marked the beginning of the union’s accountability to students.

“Satya Niketan is the heartbeat of South Campus students, yet they constantly grapple with issues related to accommodation and basic amenities,” Mr. Sharma said in the statement.

Meanwhile, DUSU vice-president Deepanshu Shokeen visited the Vice-Chancellor’s office and said he would continue to raise issues concerning regular students and fight for justice.

In a post on X, Mr. Shokeen said, “Taking Shaheed-e-Azam Bhagat Singh as our ideal, our ‘Satyagraha’ has begun today outside the Vice-Chancellor’s office.”

Referring to the demand for more hostel seats, he said, “Until the students’ legitimate demands are met, this Satyagraha will continue. It’s a fight for rights, comrades — we will claim our rights.”

World.title: Delhi SIR: BJP, Congress seek more time for filing claims, objections
World.content:
With less than 10 days left for city residents to file claims and objections, including submission of Form 6 applications for inclusion in the final electoral roll under the special intensive revision (SIR) in Delhi, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Opposition Congress on Monday sought an extension of the September 30 deadline.

Notices have been generated for 33.1 lakh electors either for “logical discrepancies” or under the “no mapping” category. The claims and objections are to be disposed of by October 29. The final electoral roll is set to be published on November 4.

“The deadline for registering as a voter should be extended to October 15,” BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor said.

Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra said he has directed party teams and booth-level agents to assist people who have received notices and help residents fill Form 6 applications.

He said the priority was to ensure that every citizen’s name is registered in the voter list at only one place in the country.

‘Procedure not clear’

Meanwhile, a delegation of Delhi Congress leaders, led by party Booth Management Committee chairman Rajesh Garg and chairman of the Legal and Human Resources Department Sunil Kumar, met Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Ashok Kumar and sought an extension of the deadline till November 30, citing delays in issuing notices and long queues at election offices.

“The Election Commission has not been able to issue more than half the notices. Most BLOs are not clear about the procedure for accepting replies to the notices,” party Delhi unit chief Devender Yadav said.

Since August 31, 92,284 Form 6 applications and 1,484 objections seeking deletion of names have been received, according to data available on Monday.

CEO Ashok Kumar said on September 19 that the situation would be assessed and an extension sought from the EC if necessary.

World.title: Supreme Court orders fresh probe into 2012 rape-murder near Dharmasthala in Karnataka
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (September 21, 2026) ordered fresh investigation into the 2012 brutal rape and murder of a 17-year-old near the bathing ghat on the outskirts of Dharmasthala in Karnataka while expressing shock at the botched-up probe into the incident.

A fresh investigation should be concluded within a period of three months and police report shall be filed before the court concerned, the court said.

The lone accused in the case, Santosh Rao, was acquitted by a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) court in June 2023. The victim’s father had subsequently filed a writ petition in the top court. He had, however, died while the case was pending. The victim’s mother took up the fight for justice for their daughter.

Search for real culprits

“Injustice to a person who was falsely charged can always be compensated. However, injustice to the victim who was brutally raped and then murdered can never be compensated. Society would be failing in its duty if it does not provide justice to the victim of such a heinous crime by conducting a proper investigation and bringing the real culprits to book,” a Bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva observed in a 49-page judgment.

The petitioner-mother was represented by senior advocates Shobha Gupta and Sanjay Nuli in the court.

Justice Sachdeva, who authored the judgment, said a fair investigation was “as much a part of a constitutional right guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution as a fair trial, without which the trial will naturally not be fair”.

“Investigation must be fair, transparent and judicious as it is the minimum requirement of rule of law. The investigating agency cannot be permitted to conduct an investigation in a tainted and biased manner. Where non-interference of the court would ultimately result in failure of justice, the court must interfere,” the judgment stressed.

Tech-savvy SIT

The court ordered the fresh investigation and directed the State of Karnataka to constitute a tech-savvy and efficient Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by a senior police officer of the State. No officer who was part of the earlier team must be included in the SIT.

The judgment directed that Santosh Rao should not be subjected to further investigation or prosecution as he had already been tried and acquitted, and was protected under Article 20(2) (double jeopardy) of the Constitution.

“Fresh investigation shall be concluded within a period of three months and the police report shall be filed before the court concerned in accordance with law, whereafter the matter shall proceed in accordance with law,” the Supreme Court ordered.

World.title: Ram Temple donations theft case: SIT report finds 105 instances of unauthorised currency removal
World.content:
A Supreme Court Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant noted on Monday that a status report submitted by the Uttar Pradesh government’s Special Investigation Team (SIT) identified 105 instances of unauthorised currency removal captured on CCTV in the Ram Temple donations misappropriation case.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, said the probe had been “substantially concluded” and a chargesheet in the case would be filed before the court of the jurisdictional Additional Sessions Judge on or before September 25, 2026.

The court noted from the report that the role of every person allegedly involved has been assessed.

Mr. Mehta pointed out that the 90-day statutory period for investigation, which started with the first arrest in the case, was drawing to an end this week.

“Some of the accused have been identified along with details provided on the number of times they engaged in misappropriation... The status report details the analysis of CCTV footage and other materials to identify the eight accused persons. It also presents a tabulated summary of the unexplained deposits in their accounts and information about the immovable and movable assets where the stolen money was invested,” the apex court order recorded.

The status report has noted the estimated amount misappropriated by each accused individual, also noting that existing evidence suggests the suspected misappropriation of currency took place within the counting room during the process of counting and handling the currency.

Receipts generated by the TCS software for 803 valuable articles have been verified, and their relevant records have been found to be with the Temple Trust. These articles are stored in a State Bank of India locker, which was physically checked.

In so far as these articles were concerned, no discrepancies were found during the verification. However, there were 86 valuable articles in respect of which receipts have not been issued. These articles had been separately identified and physically verified.

The records relating to approximately 944.411 kg of white metal (supposed to be silver) have been sent by the Trust to Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Limited for melting. Particular allegations regarding valuable donations reported in the media and on social media were verified.

These allegations included the alleged donation of 200 kg of silver bricks, 38.288 kg of silver bricks, a silver necklace, Charan Paduka, and a donation related to the Ramcharitmanas. The involved individuals have been interviewed, and the pertinent materials have been examined by them. No discrepancies were identified during this verification process.

The statements of 173 witnesses were recorded by the SIT. According to the status report, relevant Standard Operating Procedures and records relating to the counting and handling of donations, security arrangements, CCTV recordings and reconciliation records have been examined to the extent relevant to the present investigation.

The status report was perused by the Bench in court. However, the audio was muted and the screen went blank when the order was read out, requiring media personnel to enter the court room to grab shreds of the court’s oral dictation of the order.

When senior advocate Ravi Shankar Jandhyala, appearing for petitioner Ajay Kumar Rai, sought a copy of the status report, the Bench said the contents of the documents were summarised and covered in the judicial order itself.

“The State requires to be transparent,” Mr. Jandhyala said.

Reading out from the status report, the Bench said the SIT investigation was banked extensively on CCTV footage to identify the accused persons, recoveries, forensic examinations and audits.

After noting that the primary offences include criminal breach of trust and offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, the court said further investigation would continue under 193 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

Noting that though it did not want to intervene in the jurisdiction of the Sessions Court, the Bench asked the State government to file a copy of the chargesheet in the apex court too.

The next hearing will be on November 2.

The three-member SIT, headed by Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, was constituted by the State government on June 13 at the request of the Trust, before the Supreme Court intervened in the matter. Range Inspector General Kiran S. and Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar are the other members.

The FIR named eight persons — Avinash Shukla, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Kumar Yadav, Karunesh Pandey, Ramashankar Mishra, Subhash Srivastava and Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu — and other unidentified individuals as accused.

World.title: New checklist by Keralam research team records 3,261 flowering plant species in Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve
World.content:
A new checklist of flowering plants in South India’s Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve (ABR) compiled by the Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanic Garden and Research Institute (JNTBGRI) in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam, seeks to reaffirm the global significance of the Western Ghats as a biodiversity hotspot and the need for focused, region-specific strategies for protecting it.

The JNTBGRI research team documented 3,261 species, 26 sub-species and 28 varieties belonging to 1,139 genera and 190 families in the ABR. Among other things, they recorded a “high level” of endemism and biogeographic affinity with Sri Lankan and even tropical American flora. The astonishing heft of ABR’s floral wealth upholds its position as “one of the most significant centres of angiosperm diversity and endemism in the Indian subcontinent.”

Plant Science Today has published the ‘Comprehensive checklist of the flowering plants of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, South India’ compiled by E.S. Santhosh Kumar, S.M. Shareef, P.P. Anusha, K.A. Rashmi and Rejitha Joseph of JNTBGRI.

Spread over Keralam and Tamil Nadu in the southern extremity of the Western Ghats, the “hill systems and vegetation of the ABR constitute a biologically unique, yet ecologically fragile landscape,” the research paper accompanying the checklist noted.

In the ABR, Fabaceae is the most species-rich family with 349 taxa, followed by Rubiaceae (194), Poaceae (193) and Orchidaceae (168). A remarkably high level of endemism was recorded, with 1018 taxa (31.2 %) endemic to India, including 245 steno-endemic taxa (confined to highly specialised habitats). These aspects highlight ABR as both a “refugium of ancient lineages and an active centre of speciation.”

Biogeographic affinity with Sri Lanka

According to the research team, the flora here reveal “strong” biogeographic affinity with Sri Lanka, with the two regions sharing 347 taxa. Reasons may range from historical land connections during periods of lower sea level, shared Gondwanan history and long-term climatic similarities between the southern Western Ghats and Sri Lanka. Also interesting are 102 taxa displaying affinity with tropical American flora. This possibly reflects long-distance dispersal events, pan-tropical distribution patterns or naturalisation after introduction by humans, the paper said.

ABR is one of four biosphere reserves in south India – the others being the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve and the Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve. Home to some of the most diverse and fragile ecosystems in the country, these reserves are internationally noted for their high levels of endemism and species richness.

So, why a new checklist at all? For over a century, ABR has been documented through its flora, regional accounts, unpublished reports and continually evolving taxonomic databases. These collectively constitute a substantial body of knowledge. But often, they also disagree on nomenclature, taxonomic interpretation and distributional records, resulting in inconsistencies and potential misidentifications, the JNTBGRI research team argues. The present study has sought to fill this gap through an evaluation of classical flora, original and recent literature and global taxonomic repositories.

The JNTBGRI effort comes at a time when anthropogenic pressures, habitat fragmentation, climate change, biological invasion and ecological degradation are threatening many habitat-specific and narrowly distributed species in the ABR. The research team has recommended targeted, science-based and region-specific conservation strategies covering ecological restoration, ex situ conservation, long-term surveillance and community-based initiatives.

Future research, the researchers said, should ideally blend classical taxonomy with molecular phylogenetics, phylogenomics, population genetics and ecological niche modelling to “better understand the evolutionary history, diversification patterns and climate vulnerability of endemic lineages.”

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs4.61 per litre, reduces HSD rate by Rs1.96
World.content:
The government on Monday hiked the price of petrol by Rs4.61 per litre, but slashed that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.96 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs393.75 per litre while HSD will cost Rs422.08 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for Sept 22 (Tuesday).
